Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Ivanti Sentry running version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).

CVE-2026-10520 Ivanti Sentry OS command-injection in HTTP requests to admin/MICS endpoints AIExploitation High
Hunts for shell metacharacters (;, |, backtick, $(), URL-encoded variants) in HTTP requests targeting Ivanti Sentry admin/MICS service paths — the documented OS command-injection sink in CVE-2026-10520. Article-specific: targets the public PoC pattern Shadowserver reports being weaponised at scale against Internet-exposed Sentry instances. Rationale: Article states the vulnerability is an OS command injection (T1190 → T1059) and that a public PoC is being weaponised against Internet-exposed Sentry admin portals. Sentry's historical attack surface is /mics/services/* on 8443 — pairing those paths with shell metacharacters yields very low FP outside scanner traffic.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb.All_Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Authorised vulnerability scanners (Tenable, Qualys, Rapid7, Nuclei) probing CVE-2026-10520 from approved source ranges
  • Penetration-test source IPs running the public PoC against own assets
  • Sentry self-monitoring health probes that happen to include encoded query strings
  • Legitimate admin URL with a literal pipe character in a config value (rare)
Suppression filter
| where SourceIP !in ("10.0.0.0/8", "<vuln-scanner-cidrs>") and RequestClientApplication !has_any ("Nessus", "Qualys", "Nuclei", "Nmap")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: confirm the target host is an Ivanti Sentry appliance and pull the full RequestURL + response code; benign scanners almost always come from a known IP range and produce a 403/404 burst rather than 200. Step 2 — Contain: if the response is 200 and the source IP is not on the scanner allowlist, block the source at the perimeter, isolate the Sentry appliance from the internal estate, and snapshot for forensics. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on the Sentry hostname for new outbound connections, shell spawn from gateway/Java services (UC2), and authorized_keys/cron modifications (UC3) in the 24h post-request window.
CommonSecurityLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DestinationPort in (443, 8443)
| where RequestURL has_any ("/mics/", "/sentry/", "MICS", "admin")
| where RequestURL has_any (";", "|", "`", "$(", "%3B", "%7C", "%60", "%24%28", "%26%26")
| project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, DestinationIP, DestinationPort, RequestMethod, RequestURL, RequestClientApplication, DeviceVendor, DeviceProduct, Message
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Ivanti Sentry gateway/Java service spawning interactive shell or LOLBin (post-CVE-2026-10520 RCE) AIInstallation High
Detects the post-exploitation footprint of CVE-2026-10520: the Sentry web/Java service (tomcat/java/httpd/nginx) spawning bash/sh, curl, wget, nc, python or perl as a child process. Article-specific: maps to the 'execute code with root privileges' outcome and the backdoor-installation step Shadowserver observed on most exposed instances. Rationale: Article states CVE-2026-10520 yields 'code with root privileges' — the universal post-exploit tell on a Linux gateway is the web/Java service spawning a shell or curl/wget/nc to stage a backdoor (which Shadowserver confirmed has happened on 'most' exposed instances). Parent=service + child=shell/LOLBin is a near-zero-FP pair on an appliance.
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor hotfix or patch installer scripts spawning bash/curl as part of the upgrade (correlate with maintenance windows)
  • Sentry health checks invoking curl to localhost endpoints
  • Legitimate admin SSH session that itself spawned an interactive shell (rule out via InitiatingProcessParent chain)
  • Container/orchestrator probes if the gateway is containerised
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has_any ("hotfix", "upgrade", "healthcheck", "localhost")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: pull the full process chain (Java → shell → next process) and the inbound HTTP request that immediately preceded the spawn (cross-ref UC1). Confirm DeviceName is genuinely a Sentry appliance, not a dev workstation named 'sentry'. Step 2 — Contain: isolate the appliance from internal networks (block egress at perimeter, leave management VLAN), preserve volatile memory and the /tmp/ working directory, rotate any credentials handled by the gateway (MDM enrolment tokens, backend service accounts). Step 3 — Hunt: enumerate new SSH authorized_keys entries (UC3), new cron/systemd units, outbound connections to non-corporate IPs in the last 30 days from this host, and pivot on the source IP from UC1 across the rest of the estate.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("java", "tomcat", "httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "catalina.sh")
| where FileName in~ ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl", "ruby")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, ProcessIntegrityLevel, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
imProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("java", "tomcat", "httpd", "nginx", "apache2", "catalina")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash", "sh", "dash", "zsh", "curl", "wget", "nc", "ncat", "python", "python3", "perl")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Backdoor persistence on Ivanti Sentry: SSH authorized_keys modification or new cron/systemd unit AIInstallation High
Detects the persistence mechanisms Shadowserver observed on backdoored Sentry gateways: unauthorised SSH public-key additions to root or service accounts, new cron jobs, or new systemd unit files written post-exploitation. Article-specific: 'attackers had already backdoored most of the Sentry gateways exposed online' — the persistence write is the strongest survival signal once initial access has succeeded. Rationale: Article explicitly reports the gateways were 'backdoored' — on Linux appliances the canonical persistence primitives are SSH authorized_keys, cron, and systemd. Writing to any of these on a hardened gateway by anything other than the vendor patcher is a high-fidelity backdoor signal.
ATT&CKT1098.004 T1053.003 T1543.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Vendor patch (R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) installer rewriting systemd units
  • Authorised configuration-management (Ansible) push from a known control plane
  • Legitimate sysadmin rotating their own SSH key via change-controlled process
  • Internal SOAR playbook that drops a forensics-collection cron
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("ansible", "puppet", "chef-client", "yum", "dnf", "rpm", "dpkg", "apt")
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: read the file content (authorized_keys → diff against last known-good; cron/systemd → read the command it runs). If the entry runs an outbound connection, a base64 payload, or references /tmp/, treat as confirmed backdoor. Step 2 — Contain: remove the unauthorised key/cron/unit (capture content first), rotate root and all service-account credentials, terminate active SSH sessions originating from non-corporate IPs, and isolate the appliance. Step 3 — Hunt: pivot on any IP in the dropped authorized_keys / cron command across estate-wide netflow, search for the same key fingerprint on other appliances, and check for matching CVE-2026-10520 exploitation hits in UC1 within ±24h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where DeviceName has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has_any (@"/.ssh/", "/root/.ssh/") and FileName has "authorized_keys")
   or (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/var/spool/cron/"))
   or (FolderPath has_any ("/etc/systemd/system/", "/lib/systemd/system/") and FileName endswith ".service")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
imFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where DvcHostname has_any ("sentry", "mics", "mobileiron")
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/.ssh/authorized_keys", "/root/.ssh/", "/etc/cron.d/", "/etc/cron.hourly/", "/etc/cron.daily/", "/var/spool/cron/", "/etc/systemd/system/", "/lib/systemd/system/")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

id: 8a1f4e3b-2c7d-4e9f-a1b2-c3d4e5f6a703
description: Detects file writes installing persistence on an Ivanti Sentry appliance — authorized_keys additions, cron job drops, or systemd unit creation — consistent with the post-CVE-2026-10520 backdoor wave reported by Shadowserver.
references:

detection:
  selection_ssh:
    TargetFilename|contains:

  selection_cron:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - /etc/cron.d/
      - /etc/cron.hourly/
      - /etc/cron.daily/
      - /var/spool/cron/
  selection_systemd:
    TargetFilename|startswith:
      - /etc/systemd/system/

falsepositives:

source:linux.auditd @host.name:(*sentry* OR *mics* OR *mobileiron*) (@file.path:*\.ssh/authorized_keys* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.d/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.hourly/* OR @file.path:/etc/cron.daily/* OR @file.path:/var/spool/cron/* OR @file.path:/etc/systemd/system/*.service OR @file.path:/lib/systemd/system/*.service)

Ivanti Sentry running version vulnerable to CVE-2026-10520 (pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for any Sentry instance whose installed version is older than the fixed releases (R10.5.2, R10.6.2, R10.7.1). Article-specific: these are the exact patched versions Ivanti shipped Tuesday and Shadowserver warns anything older is 'most likely compromised'. Pairs with UC1/2/3 to scope blast radius. Rationale: Article names the exact fixed versions (R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1) and Shadowserver's warning that unpatched = compromised — turning the version list into a TVM/asset query is a deterministic prerequisite for scoping. Internet-facing flag prioritises the immediately-exposed subset.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Air-gapped or lab Sentry instances that legitimately run older versions
  • Decommissioned-but-still-inventoried appliances
  • Defender TVM lag — version field not yet refreshed after a same-day patch
  • CMDB stale entry where the appliance has actually been retired
Response runbook
Step 1 — Triage: sort the result by IsInternetFacing=true and confirm each hit is a live, reachable Sentry. Cross-check with perimeter logs for hits on port 443/8443 from the public internet in the last 7 days. Step 2 — Contain: emergency-patch Internet-facing instances first (Ivanti R10.5.2 / R10.6.2 / R10.7.1 per branch); for any that cannot be patched immediately, drop the admin port at the edge until patched. Step 3 — Hunt: for every vulnerable Internet-facing host, run UC1 (exploitation), UC2 (post-exploit shell), and UC3 (persistence) over the window between the CVE-disclosure date and the patch-applied time, and treat any hits as confirmed compromise per Shadowserver guidance.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-10520"
   or (SoftwareVendor in~ ("ivanti", "mobileiron") and SoftwareName has "sentry")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) on DeviceId
| project DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId == "CVE-2026-10520"
   or (SoftwareVendor in~ ("ivanti", "mobileiron") and SoftwareName has "sentry")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by DeviceId | project DeviceId, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceId, DeviceName, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, IsInternetFacing, PublicIP
| order by IsInternetFacing desc
APPLICATION
| inputlookup asset_inventory.csv
| search (vendor="Ivanti" OR vendor="MobileIron") product="Sentry"
| eval major_version=case(match(version,"^R?10\.5\."),"10.5", match(version,"^R?10\.6\."),"10.6", match(version,"^R?10\.7\."),"10.7", true(),"other")
| eval vulnerable=case(major_version="10.5" AND version!="R10.5.2","yes", major_version="10.6" AND version!="R10.6.2","yes", major_version="10.7" AND version!="R10.7.1","yes", true(),"no")
| where vulnerable="yes"
| table host, ip, vendor, product, version, owner, last_patched

Ransomware-style mass file rename / extension change Actions on Objectives Medium
Threshold detection: many files renamed in short window, often with new extension.
ATT&CKT1486
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where ActionType in ("FileRenamed","FileModified")
| summarize files = dcount(FileName) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, bin(Timestamp, 1m)
| where files > 200    // empirical: > 200 unique-file renames in 1m by one account on one host
                       //            is well above the P99 of legitimate bulk-tooling

CISA KEV: CVE-2026-10520 — Ivanti Sentry OS Command Injection Vulnerability

CISA KEV
2026-06-11 1 use case 1 technique 2 kill-chain phases detected

Ivanti Sentry (formerly known as MobileIron Sentry) contains an OS command injection vulnerability which could allow a remote unauthenticated user to achieve root-level remote code execution. This vulnerability can be successfully exploited in cases where the Sentry appliance is in an unmanaged state with its endpoints externally reachable. The use of mTLS with EPMM or restricted HTTPS access through Neurons for MDM makes interfaces inaccessible to external actors. Vendor: Ivanti, Product: Sentry. Federal patch due: 2026-06-14.

Langflow CVE-2026-5027 exploit chain: /api/v1/auto_login token then POST /api/v2/files AIExploitation High
Detects the documented exploitation pattern for CVE-2026-5027 where an unauthenticated attacker first hits Langflow's auto-login endpoint to mint a session token, then within seconds POSTs to /api/v2/files to write an arbitrary file via the unsanitised filename multipart parameter. Correlating both URIs from the same source IP within a tight window is far higher fidelity than alerting on either endpoint individually. Rationale: Article explicitly names both URIs (POST /api/v2/files for the traversal, plus the unauthenticated auto-login step that mints the session token in 'a single unauthenticated request'). Pairing them in a same-source-IP / same-host time-window correlation eliminates the noise of either endpoint hit alone. Tenable TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC (github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027) both confirm the two-step pattern. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/ • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vulnerability scanners (Tenable Nessus, Qualys, Rapid7) probing the auto_login + file upload endpoints during authenticated scans
  • Langflow integration tests / CI pipelines that exercise the auto_login + file upload flow against a staging instance
  • Developer demo flows where a single user logs in and immediately uploads a flow JSON
  • Bug-bounty researchers / red-team engagements pre-notified to the SOC
Suppression filter
| where SrcIpAddr !in ("<scanner_ip_1>","<scanner_ip_2>") | where HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent !has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Rapid7","InsightVM")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the SrcIpAddr's geo and reputation, the User-Agent string, and the HTTP response code for the /api/v2/files POST (200 = file written, 403 = blocked). If response is 200, treat as confirmed compromise. 2) Contain: take the Langflow instance offline or front it with a WAF rule blocking POST /api/v2/files where filename contains '../'; rotate any secrets reachable from the Langflow host (API keys, OpenAI tokens, MCP creds). 3) Hunt: pivot on the destination host's DeviceFileEvents/FileWritten for files written by python/uvicorn outside the Langflow data dir (UC2), and check the host's process tree (UC3) for shells spawned from the langflow process. Confirm version is <1.9.0 (UC4) and upgrade to 1.10.0.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let WindowSec = 120s;
let TokenHits = ImWebSession
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
    | where Url has "/api/v1/auto_login"
    | project TokenTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr;
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "/api/v2/files"
| project UploadTime = TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| join kind=inner TokenHits on SrcIpAddr, DstIpAddr
| where UploadTime between (TokenTime .. TokenTime + WindowSec)
| extend DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', UploadTime, TokenTime)
| project TokenTime, UploadTime, DelaySec, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, DstIpAddr, Url, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent
| order by UploadTime desc

Langflow Python process writes file outside data dir (CVE-2026-5027 post-exploit drop) AIInstallation High
Once the path-traversal write succeeds, the Langflow worker (python/uvicorn/gunicorn) is the process that writes the attacker-controlled file. Hunts for files written by that process to high-value system paths or with extensions/names indicating webshells, cron persistence, or SSH key implantation. Catches the post-exploit drop even when web/WAF logs aren't ingested. Rationale: Article confirms the impact is 'write arbitrary files on exposed servers' and VulnCheck honeypots observed 'test files' being dropped. The Langflow worker process is the only legitimate writer to its data directory, so a write by that process to /etc/, web roots, SSH key files, or cron from this process is the clean exploit indicator. Avoids false-positives on legitimate flow saves by anchoring on path/extension rather than just process identity. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1098.004 T1053.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Langflow legitimately writing user-uploaded flow JSON or RAG corpus files to a non-standard data directory configured via LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR
  • Langflow component that writes logs to /var/log via a custom logging handler
  • Python pip install/upgrade of Langflow plugins writing into site-packages (often under /usr/local/lib/python*/)
  • Backup/sync tools running as the langflow service user touching shared paths
  • Custom-flow component using python-shell or os.system to legitimately write artefacts
Suppression filter
| where not (TargetFilePath has "site-packages" and TargetFileName endswith ".py") | where ActorUsername != "root" or TargetFilePath !startswith "/var/log/langflow"
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the dropped file and check VT/Defender verdict; examine the file content directly (cat the .php / .sh / authorized_keys) for webshell magic strings or attacker SSH keys. Cross-reference Timestamp with web-log POSTs to /api/v2/files (UC1) from external IPs within ±2 minutes. 2) Contain: quarantine the file, kill the Langflow worker process, rotate the service account, remove any added SSH keys / cron entries / WAR files, and block the source IP at the perimeter. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceProcessEvents for any child process spawned by the langflow worker (UC3); look for outbound connections from the langflow process to non-RFC1918 IPs in DeviceNetworkEvents in the prior 24h.

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,

| order by Timestamp desc

Langflow worker spawns shell or LOLBin child (CVE-2026-5027 RCE) AIExploitation High
Path-traversal-to-RCE on Langflow typically ends with the python/uvicorn worker spawning a shell (bash/sh/cmd) or download utility (curl/wget) to fetch a second-stage payload after the implant lands. Detects any non-python child of the langflow worker process — Langflow legitimately runs sub-pythons only. Rationale: Tenable's TRA-2026-26 and the public PoC both demonstrate the path traversal escalating to RCE by writing an executable file the langflow worker later invokes — or by the upload handler triggering interpreter execution. Langflow's worker should only ever spawn other python interpreters (subprocess pools); a bash/curl/wget child of the langflow worker is a strong RCE indicator. Anchoring on parent cmdline containing 'langflow' avoids FPs from arbitrary python scripts on the box. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://github.com/yahiahamza/CVE-2026-5027 • https://www.securityweek.com/hackers-exploit-langflow-vulnerability-for-remote-code-execution/
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.003 T1190 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Custom Langflow component that legitimately shells out (e.g. a flow node that runs a local CLI tool — git, ffmpeg, pandoc)
  • Langflow startup script using bash to source env vars or do tini-style init
  • Healthcheck probes that exec curl from the Langflow container to test connectivity
  • Developer using `langflow run` interactively in a terminal where the parent shell is recorded as parent of python
  • Backup component shelling out to tar/gzip from within a flow
Suppression filter
| where ProcessCommandLine !has "healthcheck" and ProcessCommandLine !has "--version" | where not (FileName in~ ("curl","wget") and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("pypi.org","files.pythonhosted.org","huggingface.co"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: examine the ProcessCommandLine — look for base64 blobs, IPs/URLs being fetched, or output redirection to /tmp/.X paths. Pull the SHA256 of any downloaded file and check VT. 2) Contain: kill the Langflow process tree, snapshot the host, isolate via Defender or EDR isolation. Pull memory if a payload is likely in-memory only. 3) Hunt: identify all hosts running Langflow <1.9.0 (UC4) and check each for the same parent-child shape in the prior 14 days; pivot on outbound DeviceNetworkEvents from the langflow worker for any non-pip/non-PyPI destinations.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("python","python3","python.exe","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where FileName in~ ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o","socket.socket")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
let LookbackDays = 7d;
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("python","uvicorn","gunicorn")
| where ParentProcessCommandLine has_any ("langflow run","uvicorn langflow","-m langflow","langflow_backend")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("bash","sh","dash","zsh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","perl","ruby")
   or ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("base64 -d","chmod +x","/tmp/.","wget http","curl -o")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, MD5, SHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Langflow versions present in estate (CVE-2026-5027 exposure) AIReconnaissance High
Asset-hunting query to surface every host running Langflow <1.9.0 (or langflow-base <0.8.3) — the versions vulnerable to CVE-2026-5027 and the related Langflow CVEs (CVE-2026-0770, CVE-2026-21445, CVE-2026-33017, CVE-2025-3248). Combines Defender TVM data with live process telemetry because pip-installed Langflow may not always be in the software inventory. Rationale: Article specifies the exact version boundaries: langflow-base <0.8.3 and Langflow <1.9.0 vulnerable; 1.10.0 is the latest. Cross-checked Tenable TRA-2026-26 and Snyk advisory. ~7,000 publicly-exposed instances per Censys means most orgs running it likely have unpatched copies — making asset discovery the first defensive priority. Combining TVM CveId lookup with live process telemetry covers both inventoried installs and shadow-IT pip installs that TVM may miss. Cross-checked against: • https://www.tenable.com/security/research/tra-2026-26 • https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/unpatched-langflow-flaw-cve-2026-5027.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A test/staging Langflow instance intentionally pinned to an older version for regression testing
  • Air-gapped Langflow instance that doesn't reach the public internet (still worth patching but lower priority)
  • A Langflow fork or downstream redistribution that carries vendor backports of the fix without bumping the version string
  • DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities lag — recently-patched hosts may still show as vulnerable for up to 24h after KB sync
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the version observed by SSH'ing to a sample host and running `langflow --version` or `pip show langflow`. 2) Contain: for any exposed (internet-facing) instance, immediately gate behind a WAF or VPN, disable LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN by setting LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, and enforce LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER. 3) Hunt: for every vulnerable host in the list, run UC1 (web log chain), UC2 (file write), and UC3 (process spawn) against the last 30 days to confirm none have already been exploited; prioritise upgrade to 1.10.0.

Miasma 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' GitHub repo creation across dev accounts AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the simultaneous appearance of a repository named 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' across multiple developer GitHub accounts in a tenant — the exact naming convention SafeDep observed during the leak. Indicates compromised developer accounts being used as a leak distribution channel. Rationale: The repo name 'Miasma-Open-Source-Release' is named verbatim in the article as the exact string used across compromised accounts; near-zero collision in any legitimate dev workflow. Corroborated via SafeDep write-up referenced in the article. Cross-checked against: • https://safedep.io/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1213/003/
ATT&CKT1213.003 T1199
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Change.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Threat-intel analyst forking the leaked repo into an internal mirror
  • Detection engineer creating a honey-repo with this exact name
  • Wiki/docs page that templates the string as a literal example
Suppression filter
| where not (AccountDisplayName has_any ("security-research", "threat-intel", "detection-eng"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the creating account is owned by a real employee and check whether the same account also created the repo on personal+work GitHub identities, plus review login origin (IP, device, MFA status) for the 24h before creation. 2) Contain: rotate the account's GitHub PAT and SSH keys, revoke all OAuth grants, force re-MFA, and remove the repository from public visibility while preserving content for IR. 3) Hunt: pivot on the same actor IP across CloudAppEvents/AADSignInEventsBeta for other write actions (Actions workflow edits, package publish, secret reads); enumerate all repos created in the past 7 days with similar naming.

Miasma persistence: systemd user service or macOS LaunchAgent dropped by dev run AIInstallation High
Miasma installs its dead-man-switch monitor as a systemd user service on Linux (~/.config/systemd/user/) or a LaunchAgent on macOS (~/Library/LaunchAgents/). Detects file creation in those paths by a non-package-manager parent — a strong indicator on a developer endpoint. Rationale: Direct quote: 'The monitor runs as a systemd user service on Linux or a LaunchAgent on macOS.' These two paths are the canonical user-level persistence locations on each OS. Filtering on non-package-manager parents removes the bulk of legit installs. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1543/002/
ATT&CKT1543.002 T1547.013 T1543.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Homebrew cask install dropping a LaunchAgent for an updater (e.g. Google Software Update)
  • VS Code installing its background telemetry LaunchAgent on first run
  • Snap or Flatpak post-install hooks dropping systemd --user units
  • Developer hand-writing a personal automation .service for syncthing or restic backups
  • Configuration management (Ansible, Chef) provisioning user-level services
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("homebrew", "brew install", "vscode", "code-insiders", "ansible", "chef-client"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the .service / .plist contents and the SHA256 of the ExecStart / ProgramArguments binary; check VirusTotal and run `systemctl --user status` / `launchctl list` to confirm it's loaded. 2) Contain: `systemctl --user disable --now <unit>` or `launchctl bootout gui/<uid>/<label>` to stop the monitor, then delete the unit file; rotate any GitHub PATs and AWS keys on the host since the dead-man switch implies stolen tokens exist. 3) Hunt: search DeviceProcessEvents for invocations of the same binary, look for sibling Miasma artefacts (rm -rf ~/ in shell history, gh CLI calls), and check whether the same SHA256 dropped on other dev endpoints in the past 72h.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (FolderPath has "/.config/systemd/user" and FileName endswith ".service")
    or (FolderPath has "/Library/LaunchAgents" and FileName endswith ".plist")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("systemctl","launchctl","apt","apt-get","dpkg","brew","snap","dnf","yum","installer","softwareupdate"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where (TargetFilePath has "/.config/systemd/user" and TargetFilePath endswith ".service")
    or (TargetFilePath has "/Library/LaunchAgents" and TargetFilePath endswith ".plist")
| where not (ActingProcessName in~ ("systemctl","launchctl","apt","apt-get","dpkg","brew","snap","dnf","yum"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects creation of systemd user services under ~/.config/systemd/user/ or LaunchAgent plists under ~/Library/LaunchAgents/ — the persistence vector used by the Miasma worm's dead-man-switch monitor.

#event_simpleName=FileWritten

Miasma dead-man switch: rm -rf ~/ ; rm -rf ~/Documents on token revocation AIActions on Objectives High
The leaked Miasma 'dead-man switch' executes the exact command 'rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' when its stolen GitHub token is revoked. Detects this verbatim destructive command (or the syscall pair targeting $HOME and $HOME/Documents) from a non-interactive parent. Rationale: The article's verbatim code block 'rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' is the exact attacker signature; pairing with parent-process exclusion of common build tools (which legitimately rm -rf working dirs) removes the obvious FPs without losing the kill-switch trigger. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1485/
ATT&CKT1485 T1529 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually cleaning a stale home-clone via 'rm -rf ~/oldrepo' (won't match — needs bare ~/)
  • Dotfile reinstall scripts wiping ~/Documents-style folders
  • Docker entrypoint scripts cleaning a mounted home
  • Test-harness teardown that resets a sandbox HOME (should be in container, parent filter catches)
  • User running a stupid cleanup one-liner from Stack Overflow
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("docker run", "docker-compose", "act -", "github actions"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: snapshot or freeze the endpoint immediately; pull the parent process tree (`ps auxf` history if available, plus shell history in /root/.bash_history backups) and identify the dropping binary's SHA256. 2) Contain: kill the parent process tree before deletion completes; if completed, mount the disk read-only and begin file-carving; revoke ALL GitHub PATs / SSH keys / cloud credentials present on the host since their compromise is the trigger condition. 3) Hunt: search for the dead-man-switch unit file (~/.config/systemd/user/*.service, ~/Library/LaunchAgents/*.plist) before it self-removes; pivot on the GitHub token-revocation event timeline to find the revoked PAT and review its prior 72h of API calls for exfil patterns.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("rm","bash","sh","zsh","dash","fish")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf?\s+(~/?|\$HOME/?|/home/[^\s]+/?)(\s|;|$)"
   or ProcessCommandLine has_all ("rm","-rf","~/Documents")
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("make","cargo","go","npm","yarn","pnpm","gradle","mvn","bazel","cmake","docker","podman"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActingProcessName in~ ("rm","bash","sh","zsh","dash","fish") or TargetProcessName in~ ("rm")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)rm\s+-rf?\s+(~/?|\$HOME/?|/home/[^\s]+/?)(\s|;|$)"
    or ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("rm", "-rf", "~/Documents")
| where not (ParentProcessName in~ ("make","cargo","go","npm","yarn","pnpm","gradle","mvn","bazel","cmake","docker","podman"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Miasma dead-man switch - recursive deletion of user home directory
id: 7e2f4a1b-8c3d-4e5f-a1b2-3c4d5e6f7a01
description: Detects the verbatim 'rm -rf ~/; rm -rf ~/Documents' command emitted by Miasma's GitHub-token dead-man switch when the stolen token is revoked.
references:

author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12

source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:EXECVE @process.command_line:(*"rm -rf ~/"* OR *"rm -rf $HOME"* OR *"rm -rf ~/Documents"*) NOT (@process.parent.name:(make OR cargo OR npm OR yarn OR pnpm OR gradle OR docker OR podman))

Miasma credential fan-out: single process reading 3+ developer secret stores AIActions on Objectives Medium
Miasma harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores. Detects a single process opening three or more distinct credential-store files within a short window — the harvest signature, not the legitimate single-CLI lookup. Rationale: Article: 'harvests credentials from cloud providers, CI/CD systems, password managers, Kubernetes, and secret stores' — distinctive because a single process touches multiple unrelated store types in <1h, which legitimate tools (each scoped to one store) do not. The 3-store threshold avoids FP from `git config --global` reading both .gitconfig and .netrc. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1552/001/ • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/005/
ATT&CKT1552.001 T1555.005 T1528 T1552.007
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Dotfile sync tool (chezmoi, yadm, mackup) backing up the whole home dir
  • Antivirus full-disk scan reading every file once
  • Backup agent (Time Machine, restic, borg, duplicity) snapshotting home
  • Enterprise DLP agent inspecting credential files
  • Cloud-config CLI that legitimately reads both ~/.aws and ~/.kube during 'deploy' (filter narrows to non-CLI parents)
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("chezmoi", "yadm", "mackup", "restic", "borg backup", "timemachine", "defender_av"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcessId binary (SHA256), check signing status, and dump its open-file table to see what else it touched in the last hour; query the parent chain for unusual launchers (rundll-equivalent on linux: bash -c, python -c, node -e). 2) Contain: kill the process; rotate every credential listed in SampleStores at the issuer (AWS keys, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, kube tokens); revoke SSH key trust on every target in ~/.ssh/known_hosts. 3) Hunt: pivot on the binary's SHA256 across the fleet; check ImNetworkSession for any egress in the same window (Miasma uses GitHub as C2 — look at api.github.com POSTs); audit GitHub Actions for any workflow run by these credentials in the past 24h.
let lookback = 1h;
let stores = dynamic(["/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/config","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.pypirc","/.gem/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.gitconfig","/.netrc","/1Password","/LastPass","/Bitwarden","/.config/jfrog"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(lookback)
| where ActionType in ("FileAccessed","FileModified","FileCreated")
| where FolderPath has_any (stores) or FileName has_any (stores)
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("aws","gh","kubectl","docker","helm","git","ssh","ssh-agent","1password","op","bitwarden-cli","bw"))
| summarize StoresHit = dcount(FolderPath), SampleStores = make_set(FolderPath, 10), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, InitiatingProcessId, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| where StoresHit >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
let lookback = 1h;
let stores = dynamic(["/.aws/credentials","/.aws/config","/.ssh/id_","/.ssh/config","/.kube/config","/.docker/config.json","/.npmrc","/.pypirc","/.gem/credentials","/.config/gh/hosts.yml","/.gitconfig","/.netrc","/1Password","/LastPass","/Bitwarden","/.config/jfrog"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(lookback)
| where EventType in ("FileAccessed","FileModified","FileCreated")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (stores)
| where not (ActingProcessName in~ ("aws","gh","kubectl","docker","helm","git","ssh","ssh-agent","op","bw"))
| summarize StoresHit = dcount(TargetFilePath), SampleStores = make_set(TargetFilePath, 10), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by DvcHostname, ActingProcessId, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| where StoresHit >= 3
| order by LastSeen desc
source:(linux.auditd OR osquery) @file.path:(*/.aws/credentials* OR */.ssh/id_* OR */.kube/config* OR */.docker/config.json* OR */.npmrc* OR */.pypirc* OR */.gem/credentials* OR */.config/gh/hosts.yml* OR */.netrc* OR */1Password/* OR */Bitwarden/* OR */.config/jfrog/*) NOT (@process.name:(aws OR gh OR kubectl OR docker OR helm OR git OR ssh OR op OR bw))
#event_simpleName=FileOpenInfo
| regex("(/\\.aws/credentials|/\\.aws/config|/\\.ssh/id_|/\\.kube/config|/\\.docker/config\\.json|/\\.npmrc|/\\.pypirc|/\\.gem/credentials|/\\.config/gh/hosts\\.yml|/\\.netrc|/1Password/|/Bitwarden/|/\\.config/jfrog/)", field=TargetFileName)
| NOT (ContextImageFileName=/\/(aws|gh|kubectl|docker|helm|git|ssh|op|bw)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, ContextImageFileName], function={ count(field=TargetFileName, distinct=true, as=DistinctStores) | min(_time, as=FirstSeen) })
| DistinctStores >= 3
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.pypirc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gem/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gitconfig*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.netrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/1Password/*.sqlite*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/LastPass/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Bitwarden/*.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/jfrog/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats dc(file_path) as distinctStores values(file_path) as stores by dest user process_name process_guid | where distinctStores >= 3
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.aws/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/id_*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.ssh/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.kube/config*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.docker/config.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.npmrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.pypirc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gem/credentials*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/gh/hosts.yml*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.gitconfig*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.netrc*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/1Password/*.sqlite*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/LastPass/*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/Bitwarden/*.json*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*/.config/jfrog/*") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.process_guid | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | stats dc(file_path) as distinctStores values(file_path) as stores by dest user process_name process_guid | where distinctStores >= 3
Miasma AI coding tool config poisoning (Claude/Gemini/Cursor/Copilot/Kiro/Cline) AIInstallation Medium
Miasma poisons configuration of AI coding assistants (Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, Cline) to backdoor future code suggestions. Detects writes to those tools' on-disk config files by a non-IDE/non-installer parent process. Rationale: Article verbatim lists the six AI coding tools whose configs are poisoned (Claude, Gemini, Cursor, Copilot, Kiro, Cline). Each tool has a known config-dir convention; writes to them by non-IDE binaries are highly anomalous on a dev workstation. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1554/
ATT&CKT1554 T1546 T1647
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • User editing their Claude CONTEXT.md or .cursor/rules in VS Code via the 'code' binary (filtered)
  • Dotfile manager syncing AI tool configs (chezmoi, yadm)
  • Extension installer dropping a default settings file on first launch
  • Team-wide config push via Ansible/Munki
  • Auto-update of Copilot extension touching its settings dir
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("code", "cursor", "systemd", "launchd", "chezmoi"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: diff the modified config against the user's last-known-good version (or vendor default); look for suspicious instructions, hidden prompt-injection blocks, MCP server entries pointing to unfamiliar hosts, or auto-approve directives. 2) Contain: restore the config from backup or vendor default; rotate any AI-tool API keys stored on the host (they may also be in scope of Miasma's credential harvest); disable auto-execution / auto-approve for tools that support it. 3) Hunt: search for the dropping binary's process tree, and pivot on DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to api.github.com / api.anthropic.com / api.openai.com from non-CLI parents in the same window.
let aiConfigPaths = dynamic(["/.claude/","/.config/claude","/.gemini/","/.config/google-generative-ai","/.cursor/","/Library/Application Support/Cursor/","/.config/github-copilot/","/.vscode/extensions/github.copilot","/.kiro/","/.cline/","/.continue/"]);
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FolderPath has_any (aiConfigPaths)
| where FileName endswith ".json" or FileName endswith ".yaml" or FileName endswith ".yml" or FileName endswith ".toml" or FileName endswith ".md" or FileName endswith ".mdx"
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("code","code-insiders","cursor","cursor-helper","claude","gemini","kiro","cline","node","python","python3","brew","installer","apt","dpkg","npm","pnpm"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let aiConfigPaths = dynamic(["/.claude/","/.config/claude","/.gemini/","/.config/google-generative-ai","/.cursor/","/Library/Application Support/Cursor/","/.config/github-copilot/","/.vscode/extensions/github.copilot","/.kiro/","/.cline/","/.continue/"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where TargetFilePath has_any (aiConfigPaths)
| where TargetFilePath endswith ".json" or TargetFilePath endswith ".yaml" or TargetFilePath endswith ".yml" or TargetFilePath endswith ".toml" or TargetFilePath endswith ".md" or TargetFilePath endswith ".mdx"
| where not (ActingProcessName in~ ("code","code-insiders","cursor","claude","gemini","kiro","cline","node","python","python3","brew","installer","apt","dpkg","npm","pnpm"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

AWS SSM StartSession or aws-cli ssm from non-bastion / new caller AIActions on Objectives High
Miasma laterally moves through AWS Systems Manager (SSM) using stolen developer credentials. Detects ssm:StartSession / ssm:SendCommand calls from a principal that hasn't used SSM in the baseline, or from a non-corporate source IP — Miasma's lateral-movement signature. Rationale: Article: 'can also move laterally through SSH and AWS Systems Manager (SSM).' CloudTrail captures ssm:StartSession / SendCommand with caller identity; the anti-join against a 30-day baseline turns the noisy bulk-management noise into a first-time-caller signal. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1021/007/ • https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-logging.html
ATT&CKT1021.007 T1078.004 T1059.009
Data sourcesAuthentication.Authentication Change.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • New SRE onboarded who legitimately starts using SSM for the first time
  • CI/CD role rotation creating a new role ARN that's never used SSM before
  • Disaster-recovery drill where a break-glass role is exercised
  • Engineer's IDE plugin (e.g. AWS Toolkit) opening its first SSM port-forward session
  • Migration to SSM from SSH replacing previously-direct-SSH access patterns
Suppression filter
| where not (UserAgent has_any ("AWSCloudFormation", "AWSSSM-Patch-Baseline", "Inspector"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the full CloudTrail event for the StartSession / SendCommand including requestParameters.target (instance ID), userIdentity.arn, and sourceIPAddress; check whether the source IP is in the corp egress range or the role's normal caller geo. 2) Contain: revoke the IAM role / user's active sessions (iam:DeleteAccessKey / sts:RevokeSession), detach AmazonSSMFullAccess if unintended, and isolate the target instance via SG modification. 3) Hunt: for the same caller, enumerate sts:AssumeRole + ssm:* across the last 7 days; on the target instance, pull /var/log/amazon/ssm/amazon-ssm-agent.log and review any documents executed; pivot on developer-machine telemetry for the credential source (the harvested keys had to come from somewhere).
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession")
| extend rawData = tostring(RawEventData)
| where rawData has "ssm.amazonaws.com"
| join kind=leftanti (
    CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp between (ago(30d) .. ago(7d))
    | where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
    | where ActionType in ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession")
    | distinct AccountObjectId
  ) on AccountObjectId
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, AccountObjectId, IPAddress, CountryCode, UserAgent, ActionType, ObjectName
| order by Timestamp desc
let baseline = AWSCloudTrail
    | where TimeGenerated between (ago(30d) .. ago(7d))
    | where EventSource == "ssm.amazonaws.com"
    | where EventName in ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession")
    | distinct UserIdentityArn;
AWSCloudTrail
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventSource == "ssm.amazonaws.com"
| where EventName in ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession")
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| join kind=leftanti baseline on UserIdentityArn
| project TimeGenerated, EventName, UserIdentityArn, UserIdentityType, SourceIpAddress, UserAgent, AWSRegion, RequestParameters
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:cloudtrail @eventSource:ssm.amazonaws.com @evt.name:(StartSession OR SendCommand OR ResumeSession) @evt.outcome:success NOT @userAgent:(*aws-internal* OR *systems-manager-agent*)
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, eventSource, sourceIPAddress, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.userName, userIdentity.sessionContext.sessionIssuer.userName, userAgent, requestParameters.target, requestParameters.documentName
| filter eventSource = "ssm.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["StartSession", "SendCommand", "ResumeSession"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and userIdentity.type in ["IAMUser", "AssumedRole", "Federated", "SAMLUser"]
      and userAgent not like /aws-internal/
      and userAgent not like /systems-manager-agent/
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" All_Changes.object_category="ssm" All_Changes.action IN ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession") All_Changes.status="success" by All_Changes.user All_Changes.src All_Changes.user_agent All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | join type=left user [| tstats `summariesonly` count as baselineCount from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" All_Changes.object_category="ssm" All_Changes.action IN ("StartSession","SendCommand") by All_Changes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)`] | where isnull(baselineCount) OR baselineCount=0
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" All_Changes.object_category="ssm" All_Changes.action IN ("StartSession","SendCommand","ResumeSession") All_Changes.status="success" by All_Changes.user All_Changes.src All_Changes.user_agent All_Changes.object | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | join type=left user [| tstats summariesonly=false count as baselineCount from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where earliest=-30d@d latest=-1d@d All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" All_Changes.object_category="ssm" All_Changes.action IN ("StartSession","SendCommand") by All_Changes.user | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)`] | where isnull(baselineCount) OR baselineCount=0
Package publish (npm/PyPI/RubyGems) from compromised developer endpoint AIActions on Objectives Medium
Miasma uses stolen developer credentials to publish trojanized package versions to npm, PyPI, and RubyGems. Detects 'npm publish', 'twine upload', and 'gem push' invocations on endpoints where the user also recently accessed credential stores or hit GitHub API endpoints uncharacteristically — the worm's propagation step. Rationale: Article: 'publishing trojanized versions to infect downstream developers' via npm, PyPI, RubyGems, plus 'JFrog Artifactory instances.' Filtering out CI-runner parents focuses the detection on developer endpoints (Miasma's actual operating ground) where publish should be rare/never on a developer's workstation outside of a maintainer release. Cross-checked against: • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1195/002/
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1567
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Solo maintainer publishing a personal package from their laptop
  • Pre-release dry-run with 'npm publish --dry-run' (won't match — selection has 'publish' but real upload only)
  • Internal artifact promotion script run interactively
  • First-time package author following an npm tutorial
  • Local 'npm publish' to a Verdaccio sandbox registry
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "--dry-run") and not (ProcessCommandLine has "localhost:4873")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the package name, version, and registry URL from the command line; immediately diff the published tarball against the prior version on the registry (npm view <pkg> versions; npm pack <pkg>@<ver>) to confirm tamper. 2) Contain: unpublish (npm unpublish / pypi yank / gem yank) or mark deprecated within the 24h window; rotate the publish token; force MFA on the maintainer account; reach out to registry security if downstream installs already pulled the bad version. 3) Hunt: enumerate every other 'publish' from this user/host in the last 7 days; pivot on DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to registry endpoints from the same process to discover packages already published; check GitHub Actions workflow runs in repos owned by the user for unexpected publish steps.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("npm", "publish"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("pnpm", "publish"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("yarn", "publish"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("twine", "upload"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("gem", "push"))
    or (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("jfrog", "rt", "upload"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("jenkins","github-actions-runner","gitlab-runner","buildkite-agent","circleci-agent","runner","Runner.Listener"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("npm", "publish"))
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("pnpm", "publish"))
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("yarn", "publish"))
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("twine", "upload"))
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("gem", "push"))
    or (ActingProcessCommandLine has_all ("jfrog", "rt", "upload"))
| where not (ParentProcessName in~ ("jenkins","github-actions-runner","gitlab-runner","buildkite-agent","circleci-agent","runner","Runner.Listener"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessCommandLine, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Package publish (npm/PyPI/RubyGems) from non-CI parent
id: 9a1c5e2b-3f4d-4a8b-91c0-6d7e8f9a0b1c
description: Detects npm/pnpm/yarn publish, twine upload, gem push, or jfrog rt upload from a non-CI-runner parent — Miasma's package-trojanization vector after credential theft.
references:
  - https://www.bleepingcomputer.com/news/security/the-miasma-worm-source-code-briefly-leaked-on-github/
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1195.002
  - attack.exfiltration
logsource:
  category: process_creation
detection:
  selection_publish:
    CommandLine|contains:
      - 'npm publish'
      - 'pnpm publish'
      - 'yarn publish'
      - 'twine upload'
      - 'gem push'
      - 'jfrog rt upload'
  filter_ci:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/Runner.Listener'
      - '/gitlab-runner'
      - '/jenkins'
      - '/buildkite-agent'
      - '/circleci-agent'
  condition: selection_publish and not filter_ci
level: medium
source:(linux.auditd OR windows.sysmon OR osquery) @process.command_line:(*"npm publish"* OR *"pnpm publish"* OR *"yarn publish"* OR *"twine upload"* OR *"gem push"* OR *"jfrog rt upload"*) NOT (@process.parent.name:(jenkins OR Runner.Listener OR gitlab-runner OR buildkite-agent OR circleci-agent))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| regex("(npm|pnpm|yarn)\\s+publish|twine\\s+upload|gem\\s+push|jfrog\\s+rt\\s+upload", field=CommandLine, flags="i")
| NOT (ParentBaseFileName=/^(jenkins|Runner\.Listener|gitlab-runner|buildkite-agent|circleci-agent|runner)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, CommandLine, ParentBaseFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*pnpm publish*" OR Processes.process="*yarn publish*" OR Processes.process="*twine upload*" OR Processes.process="*python -m twine upload*" OR Processes.process="*gem push*" OR Processes.process="*jfrog rt upload*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)^(jenkins|gh-actions|gitlab-runner|github-actions-runner|buildkite-agent|circleci-agent)$")
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process="*npm publish*" OR Processes.process="*pnpm publish*" OR Processes.process="*yarn publish*" OR Processes.process="*twine upload*" OR Processes.process="*python -m twine upload*" OR Processes.process="*gem push*" OR Processes.process="*jfrog rt upload*") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where NOT match(parent_process_name, "(?i)^(jenkins|gh-actions|gitlab-runner|github-actions-runner|buildkite-agent|circleci-agent)$")
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
RMM tool installed by non-IT user — remote-access utility for hands-on-keyboard Installation High
ConnectWise / AnyDesk / TeamViewer / ScreenConnect / Atera installed outside IT change windows = common tradecraft for ransomware affiliates and IT-helpdesk impersonators.
ATT&CKT1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where FileName in~ ("AnyDesk.exe","TeamViewer.exe","TeamViewer_Service.exe",
        "ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe",
        "atera_agent.exe","SplashtopStreamer.exe","RustDesk.exe","NinjaOne.exe")
   or FileName matches regex @"(?i)kaseya.*\.exe"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where Account !endswith "$"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\AnyDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\TeamViewer_Service.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\ConnectWiseControl.ClientService.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\atera_agent.exe"

   or NewProcessName endswith "\RustDesk.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\NinjaOne.exe"

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Supply-chain trojan signal: legitimate signed binary spawning script interpreters or exotic LOLBins.
ATT&CKT1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)

File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match Installation High
Match SHA256/SHA1/MD5 named in the article against EDR file/process telemetry.
ATT&CKT1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes DeviceFileEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Pre-filter each table BEFORE the union — the engine cannot push
// predicates across `union`, and DeviceFileEvents lacks ProcessCommandLine
// (Initiating only) so column-projection has to differ per side.
union
    ( DeviceFileEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or SHA1 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or MD5 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceFileEvents" ),
    ( DeviceProcessEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(7d)
        | where AccountName !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or SHA1 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b") or MD5 in~ ("396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b")
        | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
                  Cmd = ProcessCommandLine, Source = "DeviceProcessEvents" )

// Pre-filter both ASIM tables before the union — same pattern as the
// Defender version so the engine can push hash predicates per-side.
let BadHashes = dynamic(["396cac9e457ec54ff6d3f6311cb5cc1da8054d019ce3ffa1de5741506c7a4ea4", "d8d170af3de17bb9b217c52aaaffdf9395f35ef015a57ef676e406c121e5e223", "f0641e053e81f0d01fa46db35a83e0a34494886503086866d956d14e81fd3e1c", "d5a97614d5319ce9c8e01fa0b4eb06fb5b9e54fa13b23d718174a1546444123b", "f88258e21592084a2f93a572ade8f9b91c0cd0e242f5cf6121ed7bad0f7bdd1f", "25e121e3b7d300c0d0075b33e5eca39a3e6a659fb9cfee52b70ef71686628f1b"]);
union
    ( ImFileEvent
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where TargetFileSHA256 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileSHA1 in~ (BadHashes)
           or TargetFileMD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType,
                  TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
                  Cmd = ActingProcessName, Source = "ImFileEvent" ),
    ( ImProcessCreate
        | where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
        | where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
        | where SHA256 in~ (BadHashes) or SHA1 in~ (BadHashes) or MD5 in~ (BadHashes)
        | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileName = TargetProcessName, TargetFilePath = TargetProcessName,
                  TargetFileSHA256 = SHA256,
                  Cmd = TargetProcessCommandLine, Source = "ImProcessCreate" )
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable Baileys npm package present on disk (CVE-2026-48063) AIWeaponization Medium
Hunts hosts where node_modules\baileys or node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys is present, surfacing the org's exposure to the protocolMessage / placeholderResendMessage spoofing flaw. Pivot to the package.json on hit to confirm the installed version is < 6.7.22 or in 7.0.0-rc.1..rc11. Rationale: References the exact npm package names (baileys, @whiskeysockets/baileys) and the canonical node_modules install path from the GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg advisory. Vulnerability advisories without active campaign IOCs are best served by exposure-mapping hunts — this gives the SOC a host list to drive the patching workstream. Cross-checked against the Baileys releases page where 7.0.0-rc12 / 6.7.22 are noted as the fixed versions. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/releases • https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Already-patched hosts where package.json reflects baileys >= 6.7.22 or >= 7.0.0-rc12 (analyst must read the version field to filter)
  • Developer laptops with cached test installs that are never run as long-lived sessions
  • CI/CD build agents that fetch and discard dependencies per-build
  • Docker layer scans on a host running container scanning that touch ephemeral node_modules dirs
  • Backup/restore jobs surfacing historical package.json copies
Suppression filter
// Suppress build agents and ephemeral container layers
| where DeviceName !has "build-agent"
| where FolderPath !has @"\.cache\"
| where FolderPath !has "/.npm/_cacache/"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("dockerd.exe", "containerd.exe", "docker", "containerd")
Response runbook
1) Triage: SSH/console onto the host and `cat` the matched package.json — confirm the `version` field is in the vulnerable range (< 6.7.22 OR 7.0.0-rc.1..rc11). For most matches, this is a patch-mgmt task, not an incident. 2) Contain: if the host is an internet-facing Baileys bot/integration on a vulnerable version, coordinate with the owning team to roll to 7.0.0-rc12 / 6.7.22, or apply the interim workaround (drop messages.upsert events with a `requestId` field; set `shouldSyncHistoryMessage: () => false`). 3) Hunt: pivot to UC3 to check whether any spoofed messages.upsert events have already been delivered to this host; pivot to UC2 to find recent installs that introduced the vulnerable version.
// CVE-2026-48063 — Baileys vulnerable package on-disk inventory
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified", "FileRenamed")
| where FileName =~ "package.json"
| where FolderPath has @"\node_modules\baileys\"
    or FolderPath has @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\"
    or FolderPath has "/node_modules/baileys/"
    or FolderPath has "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp),
            Installers = make_set(InitiatingProcessFileName, 10),
            InstallCmds = make_set(InitiatingProcessCommandLine, 5)
            by DeviceName, FolderPath
| order by FirstSeen asc
// CVE-2026-48063 — Baileys vulnerable package on-disk inventory (ASIM)
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated", "FileModified")
| where TargetFileName =~ "package.json"
| where TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\baileys\"
    or TargetFilePath has @"\node_modules\@whiskeysockets\baileys\"
    or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/baileys/"
    or TargetFilePath has "/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/"
| summarize FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated),
            Installers = make_set(ActingProcessName, 10)
            by DvcHostname, TargetFilePath
| order by FirstSeen asc
title: Vulnerable Baileys npm package installed (CVE-2026-48063)
id: 8f3d2b9c-1a4e-4d2f-9b6a-3c7e1d8f2a6b
description: Detects creation of package.json under node_modules/baileys or node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys, which may indicate an installation of a Baileys version vulnerable to CVE-2026-48063 (< 6.7.22 or >= 7.0.0-rc.1 < 7.0.0-rc12) — the placeholderResendMessage / fake messages.upsert spoofing flaw.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-qvv5-jq5g-4cgg
  - https://github.com/WhiskeySockets/Baileys/commit/3beb08eecfcb4e65722e674034bd84fb11a9de35
author: detection-eng
date: 2026/06/12
tags:

  - attack.t1195.001
  - attack.t1190
  - cve.2026.48063
logsource:

detection:

      - '/node_modules/baileys/package.json'
      - '/node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json'
  condition: selection
level: medium
(source:windows.sysmon OR source:linux.auditd OR source:linux.syslog) (@TargetFilename:(*node_modules\\baileys\\package.json OR *node_modules\\@whiskeysockets\\baileys\\package.json OR *node_modules/baileys/package.json OR *node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json) OR @file.path:(*node_modules/baileys/package.json OR *node_modules/@whiskeysockets/baileys/package.json))
#event_simpleName=FileWritten
| TargetFileName=/package\.json$/i
| regex("(node_modules[\\\\/]baileys[\\\\/]|node_modules[\\\\/]@whiskeysockets[\\\\/]baileys[\\\\/])", field=TargetFileName)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, TargetFileName], function=count())
