Unpatched Ivanti Sentry / FortiSandbox / SAP NetWeaver matching disclosed CVE IDs AIReconnaissance High
Inventory pivot that surfaces managed assets still running software versions vulnerable to the seven CVEs disclosed in this advisory (CVE-2026-25089, CVE-2026-10520, CVE-2026-10523, CVE-2026-44748, CVE-2026-27671, CVE-2026-22732, CVE-2026-40128). Drives patch-deployment SLA and gives the SOC a target list for compensating monitoring until patched. Rationale: Article enumerates seven CVEs with affected products and fix versions verbatim: FortiSandbox 4.4.0-4.4.8 / 5.0.0-5.0.5, Ivanti Sentry pre-R10.5.2/R10.6.2/R10.7.1, SAP NetWeaver AS ABAP, SAP Commerce Cloud, SAP Data Hub, SAP NetWeaver AS Java. Defender TVM and Sentinel's DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities tables index by CveId — exact-match pivot is reliable and gives operators a closeable list keyed to vendor patch SLAs.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Lab / test environments intentionally running unpatched versions for security research
  • Air-gapped / segmented Sentry or FortiSandbox instances scheduled in a later patch wave per change control
  • Newly-discovered devices where TVM has not yet enriched the CVE mapping
  • Decommissioned devices still appearing in inventory until removed
  • Backup/standby SAP NetWeaver systems pending coordinated outage for ABAP kernel patching
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !has_any ("lab-", "test-", "sandbox-")  // adjust to your env's non-prod naming convention
Response runbook
1. Triage: group results by CveId + SoftwareVendor; prioritise CVE-2026-10520 (CVSS 10.0 — unauth root RCE) and CVE-2026-44748 (CVSS 9.9 — SAML auth bypass) first. Cross-check whether each host is internet-facing using DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing. 2. Contain: for internet-facing unpatched Ivanti Sentry instances, place the appliance behind a temporary deny rule on `/mics/api/v2/sentry/*` until patched; for SAP NetWeaver, block external SAML SP consumer endpoint at the WAF. Open change tickets with hard SLA tied to CVSS. 3. Hunt: feed the device list into the companion detections (UC1 handleMessage hits, UC2 FortiSandbox WEB UI injection, UC3 SAP SAML XSW) and elevate any matches to incident regardless of normal triage thresholds.
let TargetCves = dynamic(["CVE-2026-25089","CVE-2026-10520","CVE-2026-10523","CVE-2026-44748","CVE-2026-27671","CVE-2026-22732","CVE-2026-40128"]);
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in (TargetCves)
| summarize FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, LastSeen desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-25089", "CVE-2026-10520", "CVE-2026-10523", "CVE-2026-44748", "CVE-2026-27671", "CVE-2026-22732", "CVE-2026-40128")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |

    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.

            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'

        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")

    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name

Endpoint exposure to CISA KEV adds: Chrome V8, Cisco SD-WAN Manager, Arista EOS (June 2026) AIWeaponization High
Inventory-driven exposure check for the three CVEs CISA added to KEV on 2026-06-10: CVE-2026-11645 (Chrome V8 OOB R/W, CVSS 8.8), CVE-2026-20245 (Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager command injection, CVSS 7.8), and CVE-2026-7473 (Arista EOS tunnel decapsulation, CVSS 6.9, no patch planned). FCEB agencies must remediate by 2026-06-23 per BOD 22-01; this UC surfaces which managed devices still carry the vulnerable software so triage can prioritise patch or mitigation. Rationale: Hard-coded to the three CVE IDs CISA explicitly added in this article (CVE-2026-11645/20245/7473). TVM tables return one row per (device, CVE) with the patched-version reference, so this is high-fidelity, near-zero-FP exposure tracking against the KEV deadline of 2026-06-23 named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190 T1203
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Device decommissioned but still reporting from cached agent telemetry
  • CVE flagged on Chrome 'beta channel' build that ships behind stable
  • Air-gapped or isolated network segments where exposure exists but exploitation is not feasible
  • TVM stale signature data hours behind actual patch deployment
  • Arista 7020R/7280R/7500R appliances not configured as tunnel endpoints (per article, exploitation requires VXLAN VTEP / GRE / decap-group config) but still flagged on version match
Suppression filter
| where SoftwareVendor in~ ("Google","Cisco Systems","Cisco","Arista Networks","Arista")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pivot on each row's Hosts list; for Chrome rows confirm browser version via DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory; for Arista rows check whether the device is actually configured as a tunnel endpoint (VXLAN VTEP, GRE, decap-group) — only those are exploitable. 2) Contain: push Chrome patch via management tool; for Cisco SD-WAN Manager apply vendor-fixed image; for Arista EOS apply the upstream/local ACL mitigation Arista published (no patch is planned). 3) Hunt: for any host that was unpatched during the public-PoC window, run the companion UC 'Chrome browser spawning LOLBin children post-V8 exploit' over the same time range to verify no exploitation occurred.

Chrome browser spawning LOLBin children post-V8 sandbox-escape (CVE-2026-11645) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts for chrome.exe spawning command interpreters or living-off-the-land binaries — the canonical post-exploitation footprint after a V8 RCE escapes the renderer sandbox. CVE-2026-11645 is described in the article as a V8 OOB R/W achieving code execution 'inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page', so the in-the-wild kill chain requires an additional sandbox escape; that escape almost always manifests as the browser process tree growing a non-Chrome child. Rationale: Pivots on the article-specific claim that CVE-2026-11645 is a V8 OOB R/W giving 'arbitrary code execution inside a sandbox via a crafted HTML page' — meaning a successful in-the-wild kill chain must escape the renderer sandbox, which manifests as chrome.exe parenting non-Chrome processes. The Defender query joins to DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory so the analyst sees the Chrome version alongside the suspicious spawn — devices that are unpatched AND showing this pattern jump to the top of the queue.
ATT&CKT1203 T1059.001 T1059.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Enterprise SSO / smartcard helpers that invoke certutil.exe from chrome.exe
  • 'Open in PowerShell' / 'Open in Terminal' from a webmail attachment context menu
  • Browser-launched MSI/EXE installers spawning a cmd /c wrapper during install
  • Chromium DevTools 'Run command' shelling to a sysadmin's preferred CLI
  • Custom enterprise browser extensions that exec helper binaries (e.g. Citrix Receiver launchers)
Suppression filter
| where not(FileName =~ "certutil.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("sso","smartcard","-user")) and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("chrome_proxy.exe","GoogleUpdate.exe","chrome_pwa_launcher.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the device's Chrome version from DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory and check it against the CVE-2026-11645 patched build. If the version is patched, the alert is almost certainly an extension/SSO false positive — close. 2) Contain: if Chrome is unpatched and the child is cmd/powershell with discovery commands (whoami, net, nltest, systeminfo) or download primitives (certutil, bitsadmin, curl), isolate the device, kill the chrome.exe tree, and collect the child process command line + SHA256 for IR. 3) Hunt: for the same device, pivot DeviceNetworkEvents on InitiatingProcessFileName == 'chrome.exe' for the last 24h to find the lure URL/IP, then sweep the org for other users who hit the same URL with an unpatched build.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "chrome.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("--type=renderer","--type=utility","--type=gpu-process")
   or isempty(InitiatingProcessCommandLine)
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe","whoami.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","nltest.exe","tasklist.exe","systeminfo.exe","qwinsta.exe","reg.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceTvmSoftwareInventory | where SoftwareName has "Chrome" | summarize ChromeVersion = any(SoftwareVersion) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ChromeVersion, ParentCmd = InitiatingProcessCommandLine, ChildBinary = FileName, ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine, ChildSHA256 = SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "\\chrome.exe"
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\\cmd.exe","\\powershell.exe","\\pwsh.exe","\\wscript.exe","\\cscript.exe","\\mshta.exe","\\rundll32.exe","\\regsvr32.exe","\\bitsadmin.exe","\\certutil.exe","\\curl.exe","\\wget.exe","\\whoami.exe","\\net.exe","\\net1.exe","\\nltest.exe","\\tasklist.exe","\\systeminfo.exe","\\qwinsta.exe","\\reg.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

| join type=inner src
    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",

                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user

Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) Exploitation High
Browser-pasted PowerShell launched from explorer/Run dialog — ClickFix social engineering.
ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents

Web probing for /dev.env or /.env exposure (CVE-2026-48031) AIReconnaissance High
Hunts for HTTP requests targeting dev.env, .env or AUTH_JWT_SECRET-bearing configuration files that would expose the hardcoded JWT secret 'random' in dhax/go-base deployments. Successful 200/301 responses indicate the file is being served and the secret is leaking. Rationale: Article explicitly names dev.env:10 as the file containing AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random and notes the secret is 'shipped to all users.' Probing this filename and seeing 200/301 is the exact discovery step preceding token forgery. Detection scopes the literal path strings from the article body. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1526 T1083 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal vuln scanners (Nuclei, Nessus, Burp scans) crawling for .env exposure during authorized assessments
  • SRE/dev probing their own staging deployments after a config change
  • Search-engine bots (GoogleBot, BingBot) following stale links to /.env that 404 historically but now 200 after a deploy slip
  • CDN cache-warm scripts pre-fetching app routes including misconfigured /.env
  • Security-headers test tools (securityheaders.com, Mozilla Observatory) walking known sensitive paths
Suppression filter
| where SrcIp !in (dynamic(["<vuln-scanner-cidrs>","<approved-pentest-ranges>"]))
| where UA !has_any ("Nessus","Nuclei","Burp","OWASP ZAP","qualys")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the matching request, response status, response size, and client IP. If status is 200 and the body contains 'AUTH_JWT_SECRET' or 'random', the secret has leaked — treat as confirmed. 2) Contain: Immediately rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32+ char openssl-generated value per PR #31 guidance, force-invalidate all existing access+refresh tokens, block the source IP at the WAF/edge, and pull the .env file out of the served web root. 3) Hunt: Search the last 30 days of access logs for any successful /.env hits from any IP, pivot on Authorization Bearer headers seen after the leak window for token claims signed with 'random', and audit admin endpoint usage (e.g. /api/v1/admin/users) from non-baseline IPs for the same period.
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any ("/dev.env","/.env","/.env.local","/.env.dev","AUTH_JWT_SECRET")
   or RemoteUrl matches regex @"(?i)/(\.env(\.[a-z]+)?|dev\.env)(\?|$)"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl","wget","python","nuclei","ffuf","gobuster","feroxbuster")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowDays = 7d;
let ProbePaths = dynamic(["/dev.env","/.env","/.env.local","/.env.dev","/.env.prod","/config/dev.env","AUTH_JWT_SECRET"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
    | where csUriStem has_any (ProbePaths) or csUriQuery has_any (ProbePaths)
    | where scStatus in ("200","301","302")
    | project TimeGenerated, Host = Computer, SrcIp = cIP, Method = csMethod, Uri = strcat(csUriStem, iff(isnotempty(csUriQuery), strcat("?", csUriQuery), "")), Status = scStatus, UA = csUserAgent, Source = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    CommonSecurityLog

    | where RequestURL has_any (ProbePaths)

    | project TimeGenerated, Host = DestinationHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, Method = RequestMethod, Uri = RequestURL, Status = EventOutcome, UA = RequestClientApplication, Source = "CommonSecurityLog"
)

title: Web Probe for dev.env or .env Exposing Hardcoded JWT Secret (CVE-2026-48031)
id: 8a7f3d54-1b2c-4e9a-9c0e-3f5b7a2d9c41
description: Detects HTTP requests targeting dev.env / .env configuration files that expose the hardcoded AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random used by github.com/dhax/go-base, enabling JWT token forgery.
references:
    - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
    - https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
    - attack.t1526
    - attack.t1083
    - attack.t1190
logsource:
    category: webserver
detection:
    selection_uri:
        cs-uri-stem|contains:
            - '/dev.env'
            - '/.env'
            - '/.env.local'
            - '/.env.dev'
            - '/.env.prod'
            - '/config/dev.env'
    selection_status:
        sc-status:
            - 200
            - 301
            - 302
    condition: selection_uri and selection_status
level: medium
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:cloudfront OR source:aws.alb) (@http.url_details.path:(*/dev.env OR */.env OR */.env.local OR */.env.dev OR */.env.prod OR */config/dev.env) OR @http.url:(*AUTH_JWT_SECRET*)) @http.status_code:(200 OR 301 OR 302)
#event_simpleName=/^(DnsRequest|HttpRequest|NetworkConnectIP4)$/
| (DomainName=/github\.com/i AND regex("dhax/go-base", field=HttpUrl)) OR regex("/dev\.env|/\.env|AUTH_JWT_SECRET", field=HttpUrl)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, HttpUrl, DomainName], function=count())
# log group: /aws/cloudfront/access OR /aws/alb/access
fields @timestamp, cs_uri_stem, cs_uri_query, sc_status, c_ip, cs_user_agent, x_host_header
| filter (cs_uri_stem like /\/dev\.env/ or cs_uri_stem like /\/\.env(\.|$)/ or cs_uri_query like /AUTH_JWT_SECRET/i)
      and sc_status in [200, 301, 302]
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.src) as src_ips values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/dev.env*","*/.env*","*/.env.local*","*/.env.dev*","*/config/dev.env*","*/AUTH_JWT_SECRET*") by Web.dest Web.url Web.status Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where status IN ("200","301","302") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.src) as src_ips values(Web.status) as statuses from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/dev.env*","*/.env*","*/.env.local*","*/.env.dev*","*/config/dev.env*","*/AUTH_JWT_SECRET*") by Web.dest Web.url Web.status Web.http_user_agent | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where status IN ("200","301","302") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
JWT token signed with hardcoded 'random' secret accepted by go-base API AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP requests bearing Authorization: Bearer tokens whose HS256 signature validates against the literal string 'random' — the hardcoded AUTH_JWT_SECRET shipped in dhax/go-base. A signature match against 'random' is unambiguous evidence of a forged admin/user token per the article's PoC. Rationale: Article PoC encodes a JWT with SECRET='random' and HS256 then hits /api/v1/admin/users, /api/v1/me, /api/v1/token/refresh. We pivot on those exact endpoints plus Python/curl/PyJWT user agents typical of forged-token tooling. Where in-app validation logs are wired up, the high-fidelity signal is a successful HS256-verify against the literal 'random' key. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/blob/master/auth/jwt/tokenauth.go
ATT&CKT1550.001 T1606.001 T1606.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web Authentication.Authentication
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate scripted API clients (CI smoke tests, monitoring synthetics) using python-requests/go-http-client against admin endpoints
  • Developers running Postman collections against /api/v1/me during feature work
  • Internal Grafana/Prometheus exporters scraping the API with go-http-client UA
  • Mobile/SPA clients that legitimately call /token/refresh on a short cadence
  • Authorized pentest using PyJWT-based token-forgery PoC tooling against the same staging endpoints
Suppression filter
| where SrcIp !in (dynamic(["<ci-runner-cidrs>","<monitoring-synthetics-ips>"]))
| where UA !has_any ("GitHubActions","Datadog Synthetics","Pingdom","UptimeRobot")
Response runbook
1) Triage: Pull the Bearer token from the offending request (if surfaced), base64-decode its payload, and attempt HMAC-SHA256 verify against the literal 'random' key — if it verifies, the token is forged. Cross-reference the claimed 'sub' / 'roles' against the IdP's user store; admin role with no matching IdP user = confirmed forgery. 2) Contain: Rotate AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a 32-byte openssl-generated value (apply PR #31), invalidate every issued access and refresh token, force re-auth org-wide, and add an edge rule to reject Bearer tokens whose 'kid'/'iss' don't match the post-rotation issuer. 3) Hunt: Replay the last 30 days of access logs for /api/v1/admin/* and /api/v1/token/refresh, decode every Bearer present, and tally how many verify against 'random' — every match is a compromised session. Audit downstream data-access endpoints touched by those sessions for exfil patterns.
// JWT-forgery via hardcoded 'random' secret — pivot on go-base API endpoints + admin claim spikes
let GoBaseEndpoints = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh","/api/v1/account"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteUrl has_any (GoBaseEndpoints)
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("Authorization: Bearer","jwt.encode","PyJWT","jose","jwtauth")
   or InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl.exe","python.exe","python3.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
let WindowDays = 7d;
let GoBaseAdminPaths = dynamic(["/api/v1/admin/users","/api/v1/admin","/api/v1/me","/api/v1/token/refresh"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    W3CIISLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
    | where csUriStem has_any (GoBaseAdminPaths)
    | where scStatus in ("200","201","204")
    | summarize Hits = count(), Endpoints = make_set(csUriStem, 20), Statuses = make_set(scStatus, 5), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Host = Computer, SrcIp = cIP, UA = csUserAgent
    | extend Source = "W3CIISLog"
),
(
    CommonSecurityLog
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(WindowDays)
    | where RequestURL has_any (GoBaseAdminPaths)
    | where EventOutcome in ("200","201","204") or DeviceAction in ("allow","allowed")
    | summarize Hits = count(), Endpoints = make_set(RequestURL, 20), Statuses = make_set(EventOutcome, 5), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Host = DestinationHostName, SrcIp = SourceIP, UA = RequestClientApplication
    | extend Source = "CommonSecurityLog"
)
| where Hits >= 1 and array_length(Endpoints) >= 1
| where UA has_any ("python","curl","PyJWT","jose","PostmanRuntime","go-http-client")
   or SrcIp !startswith "10." and SrcIp !startswith "192.168." and SrcIp !startswith "172."
| order by LastSeen desc
(source:nginx OR source:apache OR source:iis OR source:aws.alb) @http.url_details.path:(*/api/v1/admin* OR */api/v1/me OR */api/v1/token/refresh) @http.status_code:(200 OR 201) (@http.useragent:(*python* OR *PyJWT* OR *curl* OR *Postman* OR *go-http-client*) OR @http.request.headers.authorization:Bearer*)
#event_simpleName=/^(ProcessRollup2|SyntheticProcessRollup2)$/
| (regex("jwt\.encode|PyJWT|jwtauth\.New|jose\.sign", field=CommandLine) OR CommandLine=/"random"/i)
| CommandLine=/(HS256|HmacSHA256|jwt\.encode|jwtauth)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
# log group: /aws/alb/access OR /aws/apigateway/access
fields @timestamp, request_url, elb_status_code, client_ip, user_agent, request_creation_time
| filter (request_url like /\/api\/v1\/admin/ or request_url like /\/api\/v1\/token\/refresh/ or request_url like /\/api\/v1\/me/)
      and elb_status_code in [200, 201, 204]
      and (user_agent like /python/i or user_agent like /PyJWT/i or user_agent like /go-http-client/i or user_agent like /curl/i or user_agent like /Postman/i)
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.src) as src_ips from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/admin/*","*/api/v1/me","*/api/v1/token/refresh","*/api/v1/auth/*") by Web.dest Web.http_user_agent Web.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)authorization:\s*bearer\s+(?<jwt>[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)" | where isnotnull(jwt) | rex field=jwt "^(?<header_b64>[^.]+)\.(?<payload_b64>[^.]+)\.(?<sig>[^.]+)$" | eval payload=base64decode(payload_b64) | search payload="*admin*" OR payload="*roles*" | table _time dest src_ips user http_user_agent payload
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Web.url) as urls values(Web.src) as src_ips from datamodel=Web.Web where Web.url IN ("*/api/v1/admin/*","*/api/v1/me","*/api/v1/token/refresh","*/api/v1/auth/*") by Web.dest Web.http_user_agent Web.user _time | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | rex field=_raw "(?i)authorization:\s*bearer\s+(?<jwt>[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.[A-Za-z0-9_-]+)" | where isnotnull(jwt) | rex field=jwt "^(?<header_b64>[^.]+)\.(?<payload_b64>[^.]+)\.(?<sig>[^.]+)$" | eval payload=base64decode(payload_b64) | search payload="*admin*" OR payload="*roles*" | table _time dest src_ips user http_user_agent payload
go-base AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random in deployed config or compiled binary AIWeaponization Medium
Asset-exposure hunt for hosts running github.com/dhax/go-base where AUTH_JWT_SECRET is still the default 'random'. Catches .env files containing the weak value, viper config reads on serve.go startup with the default fallback path, and go-base binaries that haven't been rebuilt with the PR #31 weak-secrets map. Rationale: Article names two literal locations: dev.env line 10 (AUTH_JWT_SECRET=random) and cmd/serve.go line 35 (viper.SetDefault("auth_jwt_secret", "random")). Plus the PR #31 weak-secrets map enumerates the additional values to hunt. Hunting these exact strings on disk and in process cmdline finds vulnerable deployments before exploitation. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm • https://github.com/dhax/go-base
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1552.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Endpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer workstations cloning go-base for evaluation, never deployed
  • CI build runners that legitimately read dev.env during template testing
  • Security-scanner agents (Trivy, Grype, Snyk) reading config files for compliance reporting
  • Backup/EDR agents enumerating .env files for DLP classification
  • Internal docs/blog mentions of go-base copied into knowledge bases and indexed by enterprise search
Suppression filter
| where Path !has_any ("\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\snyk","\\trivy-cache","\\grype-cache","/var/lib/snyk")
| where ProcessName !in~ ("trivy","grype","snyk","syft")
Response runbook
1) Triage: For each match, open the file or process cmdline and confirm AUTH_JWT_SECRET literally equals 'random' (or another weak value from the PR #31 map). Identify whether the host is a production service, a staging instance, or a dev workstation. 2) Contain: For any prod/staging match, rotate the secret to `openssl rand -base64 32` output, redeploy with the PR #31 patched tokenauth.go, invalidate all issued JWTs, and gate the endpoints behind WAF token validation until rotation completes. 3) Hunt: Pull 30 days of access logs for the affected service, decode every Bearer token, and count how many verify against 'random' — each is a forged session. Audit `users` table changes, admin-endpoint hits, and refresh-token issuances during that window.
// Catch deployed dhax/go-base instances still using the hardcoded 'random' secret
let WeakSecrets = dynamic(["random","secret","changeme","change-me","default"]);
union isfuzzy=true
(
    DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where FileName in~ ("dev.env",".env",".env.local",".env.prod",".env.dev","config.env")
         or FolderPath has "go-base"
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FolderPath, FileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine

go-base service restart storm from non-persistent JWT key regeneration AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the operational symptom of the broken pre-patch mitigation: the in-memory randStringBytes(32) key resets on every restart, invalidating every active session. Repeated go-base process restarts paired with a flood of 401 responses on /api/v1/* indicates either pre-patch vulnerable behaviour OR an attacker triggering restarts to harvest fresh token-validation traces. Rationale: Article explicitly calls out that the pre-patch mitigation auto-generated a non-persistent randStringBytes(32) key on every restart, breaking every active session — 'the fix itself a denial-of-service.' A burst of go-base process restarts coincident with a 401 flood on /api/v1/* signals either the vulnerable pre-patch behaviour at scale OR adversary-induced restarts during exploitation testing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/dhax/go-base/pull/31 • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mqq6-462x-jxmm
ATT&CKT1499.004 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate rolling deploys / blue-green flips that intentionally restart go-base instances
  • Auto-scaling group scale-in/scale-out events cycling instances
  • Health-probe failures triggering systemd restart loops due to unrelated dependency outages (DB, Redis)
  • Pre-patch dhax/go-base operators routinely hitting this issue without an attacker present
  • Kubernetes node drain / cordon ops during cluster maintenance
Suppression filter
| where Host !in (dynamic(["<blue-green-deploy-hosts>"]))
| where Bucket !between (datetime(<deploy-window-start>) .. datetime(<deploy-window-end>))
Response runbook
1) Triage: For the host(s) flagged, check whether the go-base build predates the PR #31 merge (May 17 2026). If yes, the 401 storm is the documented self-DoS — escalate as a vuln-exposure ticket, not an intrusion. If patched, look for the trigger of the restarts (OOM, panic, deploy event, or attacker-induced crash). 2) Contain: If pre-patch, schedule an emergency upgrade to a post-PR-31 build, set AUTH_JWT_SECRET to a strong persistent value, and warn users that sessions were dropped. If post-patch and restarts are attacker-induced, pull stack traces / panic logs to find the crash vector and block the source IP at the WAF. 3) Hunt: Review whether any successful auth events to /api/v1/admin/* happened immediately after the restart storm — a forged admin token reissued post-restart against the in-memory key would be a high-severity indicator. Cross-check refresh-token endpoint hits during the same window.

Compromised Rust crate onering performs code exfiltration

Aikido
2026-06-10 8 use cases 3 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

The compromised onering Rust crate v1.4.1 on crates.io shipped a malicious build.rs that exfiltrates the diff of your latest commit to a hosted Sentry endpoint every time you build. Category: Vulnerabilities & Threats

ATT&CKT1176 T1190 T1195.002
Domainso4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] Cargo dependency manifest or download pinned to compromised onering 1.4.1
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → Suspicious browser extension installation
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Network egress to onering Sentry exfil ingest domain or project envelope path · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] Cargo build script spawning git with onering's exfil --pretty=format JSON · [LLM] build.rs invoking curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint with code diff payload · Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs
Cargo build script spawning git with onering's exfil --pretty=format JSON AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the onering 1.4.1 build.rs harvesting host repo metadata by spawning `git log -n 1 --pretty=format:{"commit":"%H","author":"%an",...}` from a Cargo build-script process. The JSON pretty-format template plus a Cargo build-script parent is the article-specific fingerprint of the exfil step. Rationale: Anchors on the verbatim --pretty=format JSON template strings the article shows in the build.rs payload (`commit`, `%H`, `author`, `%an`, `email`, `%ae`) combined with a Cargo build-script parent (rustc compiles build.rs to a binary named `build-script-build` on Windows/Linux). Routine `git log` calls from IDEs/CI don't carry this exact JSON tag set parented by a build-script process. Cross-checked the build-script-build naming via the official Cargo build-script reference (doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html) and the upstream maintainer issue https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/build-scripts.html
ATT&CKT1005 T1195.001 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer tooling (rust-analyzer, IDE git extensions) running git log with --pretty=format but using a CSV/tab template, not the JSON tag set above
  • CI scripts running git log --pretty=format from a shell, not parented by build-script-build
  • Custom internal Rust crates whose legitimate build.rs invokes git for version-stamping (usually only `git rev-parse HEAD`, not multi-field JSON metadata)
  • Cargo workspace tooling like `cargo-edit` or `cargo-release` shelling out to git from rustc context
  • Manual test of the cenotelie/onering repository itself by a researcher reproducing the IOC
Suppression filter
| where not (ProcessCommandLine has "rev-parse" and not (ProcessCommandLine has_all ("%H", "%an", "%ae")))
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture full process tree (cargo→rustc→build-script-build→git), the Cargo.lock and Cargo.toml on the host, and the user's home repo path; confirm `onering` 1.4.1 is in the dependency graph (`cargo tree | grep onering`). 2) Contain: isolate the dev workstation from the network, kill the cargo build, revoke any source-control PATs the user has cached (gh, git credential-manager), and force-push-protect any branches the user touched in the last 24h. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents for the same DeviceId reaching o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io or any /api/4511539669368912/envelope/ POST in the last 30 days, pivot on every other host that resolved that domain, and search Cargo.lock files repo-wide for `onering` at v1.4.1.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("git.exe", "git")
| where ProcessCommandLine has "log"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "--pretty=format"
| where ProcessCommandLine has_all ("commit", "%H", "author", "%an", "email", "%ae")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("build-script-build.exe", "build_script_build.exe", "build-script-build", "cargo.exe", "rustc.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\git.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/git"
| where CommandLine has "--pretty=format"
| where CommandLine has_all ("commit", "%H", "author", "%an")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo.exe", "rustc.exe")
| where SubjectUserName !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

build.rs invoking curl POST to Sentry envelope endpoint with code diff payload AIActions on Objectives High
Detects the onering build.rs exfiltration POST: curl invoked with the specific Sentry envelope URL (project id 4511539669368912 / org id o4511539639222272) and the `application/x-sentry-envelope` Content-Type, parented by a Cargo build-script process. This is the network-layer half of the exfil chain. Rationale: Article gives the verbatim Sentry ingest URL, DSN public key, organization id and project id. Curl parented by a Cargo build-script with any of those four strings in the cmdline is essentially deterministic for the onering payload. The combination forecloses noise from legit Sentry users (none would have curl invoked by build-script-build) and from legit Cargo builds (none would POST to a Sentry envelope). Cross-checked the Sentry envelope endpoint format at docs.sentry.io/api/envelopes/. Cross-checked against: • https://docs.sentry.io/api/envelopes/ • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1041 T1567 T1071.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Project legitimately using Sentry crash-reporting from Rust code, but invoked via the sentry-rust SDK at runtime (not via curl in a build script)
  • Developer manually testing the IOC for IR/research purposes from the same host
  • Internal Sentry-on-prem mirror where the URL happens to contain the same project id substring
  • Penetration-test simulation of supply-chain exfil using these exact IOCs
  • Threat-intel platform crawler fetching the article URL into a curl trace logged by EDR
Response runbook
1) Triage: capture the curl process tree, extract the POST body if proxy/PCAP available, and confirm the DSN public key 8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821 in the URL path. Pull Cargo.lock on the host and grep for `onering`. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill the cargo build, block o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io at the proxy, rotate any source-tree secrets the recent commit may have touched (treat the recent diff as exposed). 3) Hunt: pivot DeviceNetworkEvents on the destination domain across the fleet for the last 30 days; pivot on every internal repo whose Cargo.lock contains onering 1.4.1; alert affected dev leads that recent commits leaked.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where FileName in~ ("curl.exe", "curl")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io", "4511539669368912/envelope", "application/x-sentry-envelope", "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("build-script-build.exe", "build_script_build.exe", "build-script-build", "cargo.exe", "rustc.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith "\\curl.exe" or NewProcessName endswith "/curl"
| where CommandLine has_any ("o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io", "4511539669368912/envelope", "application/x-sentry-envelope", "8197ee42c4f59c83f4cc6d48f5bae821")
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("build-script-build", "build_script_build", "cargo.exe", "rustc.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName

Network egress to onering Sentry exfil ingest domain or project envelope path AICommand & Control High
Wire-side catch-all for hosts reaching the article's Sentry ingest domain or the project-specific `/api/4511539669368912/envelope/` path — independent of the process that initiated it (covers proxied/wrapped variants and Linux/macOS dev hosts where Cargo runs). Rationale: Article names the exact ingest hostname `o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io` and project envelope path `/api/4511539669368912/envelope/`. Domain alone is so specific that any internal DNS resolution or HTTP request to it is high-confidence — and catches process variants (the maintainer's GitHub repo is also compromised, so the payload could land via `git clone` rather than crates.io). 30-day lookback because exfil-per-commit means even one historical hit is interesting. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1567
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Project legitimately using a Sentry org with the same numeric org-id (collisions are astronomically unlikely for this specific id but technically possible)
  • Threat-intel platform proxy fetching the article or IOC bundles citing the domain
  • Detection-engineering lab host reproducing the IOC for rule tuning
  • Internal Sentry-on-prem instance whose path namespace happens to coincide (won't share the public DNS name)
  • Browser preview from analyst clicking the article URL
Response runbook
1) Triage: enrich the source host with cargo / Rust toolchain inventory and recent process tree; identify the process that owned the egress (curl vs sentry-rust SDK vs something else). 2) Contain: sinkhole `o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io` at corporate DNS and add a deny on the URL path at the egress proxy; isolate impacted hosts; treat the most recent git diff on each impacted repo as leaked and rotate any secrets it touched. 3) Hunt: dump every host that resolved the domain in the last 90 days; for each, run `cargo tree` against every repo on disk for `onering` 1.4.1; check the maintainer's GitHub repo (https://github.com/cenotelie/onering) is pinned to a vetted commit, not main.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io" or RemoteUrl has "4511539669368912/envelope"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort),
(DeviceEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
 | where AdditionalFields has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, AdditionalFields)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Url has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io" or Url has "4511539669368912/envelope"
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, DstIpAddr),
(ImDnsActivity
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where DnsQuery has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, DnsQuery, DnsResponseName),
(CommonSecurityLog
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where RequestURL has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io" or RequestURL has "4511539669368912/envelope" or DestinationHostName has "o4511539639222272.ingest.de.sentry.io"
 | project TimeGenerated, SourceIP, SourceUserName, RequestURL, DestinationHostName, DestinationIP, RequestMethod)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cargo dependency manifest or download pinned to compromised onering 1.4.1 AIDelivery Medium
Catches the supply-chain ingress: file writes to Cargo.lock / Cargo.toml mentioning the malicious crate version, or HTTPS downloads of the onering 1.4.1 crate tarball from crates.io. Targets the build-time moment when a dev pulls the poisoned dependency, before build.rs runs. Rationale: Anchors on the article's explicit IOC `onering 1.4.1 from crates.io`. Cargo writes the cache file `onering-1.4.1.crate` under `~/.cargo/registry/cache/<index>/` and updates Cargo.lock with the pinned version on resolve — both are deterministic side-effects of pulling the poisoned dep. Article also flags that the GitHub repo is compromised, so we keep the file-write detection generic enough to fire on git-cloned dependencies (where the URL fetch wouldn't trigger). Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/cenotelie/onering/issues/1 • https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/registries.html
ATT&CKT1195.001 T1195.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Security researcher or detection engineer intentionally fetching the IOC for sandboxing
  • Mirror/proxy of crates.io pre-fetching the malicious version into local cache before a yank propagates
  • Vulnerability scanner like cargo-audit or Aikido enumerating the version
  • Legacy CI pipeline still referencing onering 1.4.1 after yank but on an isolated build agent
  • Developer cleaning up `Cargo.lock` after a known-bad pull (Cargo writes the file even on `cargo update --precise` to a safe version, with onering removed)
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the host's `~/.cargo/registry/cache/**/onering-1.4.1.crate` and confirm SHA256 matches the malicious tarball; grep every repo on disk for `onering` in Cargo.lock and note the version. 2) Contain: instruct the dev to `cargo update -p onering --precise <safe-version>` or remove the dependency, force a fresh `cargo build` in a clean target dir, and on shared CI invalidate the cargo cache. 3) Hunt: across the org's source-control, run `git grep -E 'onering.*=.*"1\.4\.1"'` on every Rust repo; check internal Cargo mirrors for any hosts that pulled the bad version; coordinate with Aikido feed for org-wide blast radius.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where RemoteUrl has "crates.io" and (RemoteUrl has "onering/1.4.1" or RemoteUrl has "onering-1.4.1.crate")
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where FileName in~ ("Cargo.lock", "Cargo.toml")
 | where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("cargo.exe", "cargo")
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine),
(DeviceFileEvents
 | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
 | where FolderPath has ".cargo\\registry\\cache" or FolderPath has ".cargo/registry/cache"
 | where FileName has "onering-1.4.1"
 | project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256)
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(ImWebSession
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where Url has "crates.io" and (Url has "onering/1.4.1" or Url has "onering-1.4.1.crate")
 | project TimeGenerated, SrcHostname, SrcIpAddr, SrcUsername, Url, HttpMethod),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where TargetFileName in~ ("Cargo.lock", "Cargo.toml")
 | where ActingProcessName has "cargo"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessCommandLine),
(ImFileEvent
 | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
 | where TargetFileName has "onering-1.4.1"
 | project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256)
| order by TimeGenerated desc
(source:zeek (@http.url:*crates.io*onering\/1.4.1* OR @http.url:*crates.io*onering-1.4.1.crate*)) OR (source:linux.auditd @auditd.type:PATH @file.path:*\/.cargo\/registry\/cache\/*onering-1.4.1*) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 (@TargetFilename:*\\.cargo\\registry\\cache\\*onering-1.4.1* OR @TargetFilename:*\\Cargo.lock OR @TargetFilename:*\\Cargo.toml))
(#event_simpleName=FileWritten (TargetFileName=/onering-1\.4\.1/i OR (TargetFileName=/[\\/](Cargo\.lock|Cargo\.toml)$/i ContextImageFileName=/cargo(\.exe)?$/i))) OR (#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/(static\.)?crates\.io/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())

status: experimental

HTTP/2 Bomb mitigation tampering — MaxHeadersCount registry value (CVE-2026-49160) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Watch for write, delete, or downward modification of the new `MaxHeadersCount` registry value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters. Microsoft introduced this value specifically to mitigate the HTTP/2 Bomb DoS against IIS/HTTP.sys (CVE-2026-49160). An attacker who reaches admin on an IIS host could remove or set it to 0 to re-enable the DoS surface; conversely the value going from set→unset on a host that previously had it is a tampering signal. Rationale: Pulls the exact registry path and value name (`MaxHeadersCount` under `HTTP\Parameters`) that the article quotes Microsoft as introducing in the June 2026 update. Tamper-with-the-mitigation is a higher-fidelity signal than trying to detect the HTTP/2 Bomb payload itself on the wire, which IIS logs don't expose at header-count granularity.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1112
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sysadmin manually applying or tuning the new mitigation (legitimate IIS hardening sweep)
  • Configuration management tools (DSC / Ansible / GPO) deploying the registry value across an IIS fleet
  • Microsoft KB rollback during a problematic patch cycle
  • IIS performance team raising the limit above default for a high-header app
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("TrustedInstaller.exe","MsiExec.exe","services.exe")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull `InitiatingProcessFileName` and account; legitimate sets come from `services.exe`/`TrustedInstaller.exe` or known CM agents. Anything signed by an interactive user, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, or LOLBins is suspicious. Step 2: Contain — if change is unexpected, restore the value (>= 100 is Microsoft's default, see KB) and snapshot the IIS host. Step 3: Hunt — look back 24h on the same host for w3wp.exe spawning shells, IIS module installs (`appcmd.exe install module`), or unexpected HTTP/2 traffic spikes; pivot to the HTTP.sys/IIS anomalous-child UC.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "MaxHeadersCount"
| where ActionType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryValueDeleted","RegistryKeyDeleted")
| extend NewVal = tostring(RegistryValueData), PrevVal = tostring(PreviousRegistryValueData)
| where ActionType != "RegistryValueSet" or NewVal in ("0","0x0","") or toint(NewVal) < toint(coalesce(PrevVal,"0"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, NewVal, PrevVal,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where RegistryKey has @"\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters"
| where RegistryValue =~ "MaxHeadersCount"
| where EventType in~ ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryValueDeleted","RegistryKeyDeleted")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData,
          RegistryPreviousValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: HTTP.sys MaxHeadersCount Mitigation Tampering (CVE-2026-49160 HTTP/2 Bomb)
id: 8d1f3a72-2a2f-4b91-9e6b-f1b3d2e4a0c7
description: Detects modification or deletion of the MaxHeadersCount registry value under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters, which Microsoft introduced in the June 2026 patch as the mitigation for the HTTP/2 Bomb DoS (CVE-2026-49160). Removal or zeroing of this value re-enables the DoS surface against IIS / HTTP.sys.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-patches-record-206-flaws.html
author: thn-usecases

  - attack.t1112
  - attack.defense_evasion
logsource:

  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    TargetObject|contains: '\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\HTTP\Parameters\MaxHeadersCount'
  condition: selection
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:13 (@TargetObject:(*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\HTTP\\Parameters\\MaxHeadersCount OR *\\system\\currentcontrolset\\services\\http\\parameters\\maxheaderscount))
#event_simpleName=AsepValueUpdate
| RegObjectName=/\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\HTTP\\Parameters/i
| RegValueName=/MaxHeadersCount/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RegObjectName, RegValueName, RegStringValue, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.registry_previous_value_data) as previous_value_data values(Registry.process_name) as process_name values(Registry.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\HTTP\\Parameters*" Registry.registry_value_name="MaxHeadersCount" Registry.action IN ("modified","deleted","created") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where action!="created" OR (action="created" AND value_data IN ("0","0x0"))
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Registry.registry_value_data) as value_data values(Registry.registry_previous_value_data) as previous_value_data values(Registry.process_name) as process_name values(Registry.user) as user from datamodel=Endpoint.Registry where Registry.registry_path="*\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Services\\HTTP\\Parameters*" Registry.registry_value_name="MaxHeadersCount" Registry.action IN ("modified","deleted","created") by Registry.dest Registry.registry_path Registry.registry_value_name Registry.action | `drop_dm_object_name(Registry)` | where action!="created" OR (action="created" AND value_data IN ("0","0x0"))
DHCP Client svchost anomalous child process (CVE-2026-44815 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
CVE-2026-44815 is a pre-auth stack-overflow RCE in the Windows DHCP Client. The DHCP Client service runs in svchost.exe under the `LocalServiceNetworkRestricted` host with the `Dhcp` service argument. Successful exploitation would surface as svchost (DHCP-hosted) spawning a non-svchost child — there is essentially no legitimate reason for `Dhcp`-hosted svchost to create a shell, script host, or LOLBin. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-44815 ... allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network ... systems handling DHCP traffic should be treated as high-priority patch targets.' DHCP Client svchost normally never spawns shells; pairing the parent (`-s Dhcp` / `LocalServiceNetworkRestricted`) with the LocalService SID and a LOLBin child is a low-FP combination.
ATT&CKT1190 T1059 T1203
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Microsoft DHCP troubleshooting kits running `ipconfig.exe` under the service context
  • Endpoint management agents (Intune/SCCM) invoking `net.exe` via the DHCP host briefly during network re-init
  • MDM remediation scripts that target DHCP renewal
  • Sysinternals procdump / handle.exe by IR team taking dumps of svchost
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !has "ipconfig /renew"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the parent command line really contains `-s Dhcp` (not another svchost service); pull the SHA256 of the child and the network connections from the same `InitiatingProcessId` ±5 min. Step 2: Contain — isolate the host with Defender 'Isolate device' or NAC quarantine; capture the DHCP packet trace if still online (rogue DHCP server may be persistent on the LAN). Step 3: Hunt — across the same subnet, look for additional DHCP Client hosts that received a DHCP OFFER from the same MAC, and pivot to the patch-inventory UC for CVE-2026-44815 to find other still-vulnerable hosts on the same broadcast domain.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "svchost.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("-s Dhcp", "-s dhcp", "LocalServiceNetworkRestricted")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","net1.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe","hostname.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\svchost.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase in ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe")
| where SubjectUserSid in ("S-1-5-19","S-1-5-20")  // LOCAL SERVICE / NETWORK SERVICE — DHCP runs as LocalService
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType, ProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DHCP Client svchost Spawning Shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-44815)
id: 4c2e95ab-7f1d-4a8b-9c4e-2d3f1e6a8b04
description: Detects the Windows DHCP Client svchost host (svchost.exe -k LocalServiceNetworkRestricted -s Dhcp) spawning a shell, script host, or LOLBin — consistent with successful exploitation of CVE-2026-44815, the pre-auth stack-buffer-overflow RCE in the DHCP Client patched in June 2026.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-patches-record-206-flaws.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1059
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.execution
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent_svchost_dhcp:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\svchost.exe'
    ParentCommandLine|contains:
      - '-s Dhcp'
      - 'LocalServiceNetworkRestricted'

    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bitsadmin.exe'
      - '\certutil.exe'
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\whoami.exe'

  condition: parent_svchost_dhcp and suspicious_child
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\svchost.exe OR *\\Svchost.exe OR *\\SVCHOST.EXE)) (@ParentCommandLine:(*"-s Dhcp"* OR *"-s dhcp"* OR *LocalServiceNetworkRestricted*)) (@Image:(*\\cmd.exe OR *\\CMD.EXE OR *\\powershell.exe OR *\\PowerShell.exe OR *\\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\\pwsh.exe OR *\\mshta.exe OR *\\MSHTA.EXE OR *\\wscript.exe OR *\\cscript.exe OR *\\rundll32.exe OR *\\regsvr32.exe OR *\\bitsadmin.exe OR *\\certutil.exe OR *\\net.exe OR *\\whoami.exe OR *\\nltest.exe))

| ParentBaseFileName=/svchost\.exe$/i
| UserName=/LOCAL SERVICE/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|mshta|wscript|cscript|rundll32|regsvr32|bitsadmin|certutil|net|whoami|nltest|ipconfig)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.parent_process) as parent_cmd values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="svchost.exe" Processes.parent_process IN ("*-k LocalServiceNetworkRestricted*","*-s Dhcp*","*-s dhcp*") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","net.exe","whoami.exe","nltest.exe","ipconfig.exe") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
