Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Trusted vendor binary / installer launching unusual children
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key.
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking.
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] AWS CloudTrail trail tampering — StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or UpdateTrail disabling log validation/destination · [LLM] AWS S3 bucket deletion targeting an active CloudTrail log destination · [LLM] AWS CloudWatch Logs group deletion or retention shortened on audit-tier log groups · [LLM] GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted · [LLM] GCP Cloud Logging bucket deletion (DELETE_REQUESTED state)
AWS CloudTrail trail tampering — StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or UpdateTrail disabling log validation/destination AIActions on Objectives High
Detects defense-evasion via direct manipulation of CloudTrail trails — the article-named StopLogging API, plus DeleteTrail and UpdateTrail calls that strip log-file-integrity validation or repoint the S3 destination. These are the textbook 'blind the watchmen' actions described in Unit 42's writeup. Rationale: Article explicitly names `cloudtrail:StopLogging` as the primary 'Stop Logging' technique; reviewer extended to DeleteTrail and UpdateTrail tampering of S3BucketName / EnableLogFileValidation. All four eventNames are documented CloudTrail management APIs. The AWSService filter suppresses CloudTrail-managed lifecycle events.
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/CloudFormation pipeline rotating a trail during planned infrastructure changes
  • Security team migrating CloudTrail destination from per-account bucket to org-wide log archive bucket
  • Decommissioning an unused legacy trail during account hygiene cleanup
  • Vendor onboarding (SIEM/CSPM) recreating trails to point at vendor-managed S3 buckets
  • Disaster recovery test in a sandbox account spinning trails up and down
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has "AWSReservedSSO_ChangeMgmt" and CallerArn !has "terraform-ci" and CallerArn !has "controltower-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull the caller (userIdentity.arn), source IP, and userAgent; confirm whether the principal is a human, CI role, or AWSService. Check if a CAB / change ticket covers a trail change in this window. 2) Contain: if unauthorized, immediately re-enable the trail via StartLogging (or recreate from IaC baseline), restrict the offending principal with a temporary deny SCP/inline policy on cloudtrail:Stop*/Delete*/Update*, and rotate any access keys belonging to the principal. 3) Hunt: pivot on the principalId across all CloudTrail events for the prior 7 days for IAM persistence (CreateUser, AttachUserPolicy, CreateAccessKey), GuardDuty/Config tampering, and S3 bucket policy edits on the trail destination bucket.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("StopLogging", "DeleteTrail", "UpdateTrail")
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend TrailName = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.name),
         NewS3Bucket = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.s3BucketName),
         LogValidation = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation),
         ErrorCode = tostring(Raw.errorCode),
         CallerArn = tostring(Raw.userIdentity.arn),
         CallerType = tostring(Raw.userIdentity.type)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where ActionType != "UpdateTrail" or (LogValidation =~ "false" or isnotempty(NewS3Bucket))
| where CallerType != "AWSService"
| project Timestamp, ActionType, TrailName, NewS3Bucket, LogValidation, CallerArn, CallerType, IPAddress, CountryCode, AccountDisplayName
| order by Timestamp desc

CloudAppEvents

title: AWS CloudTrail Trail Tampered — StopLogging / DeleteTrail / UpdateTrail Weakened
id: 8d2f1c3a-4e7b-4a91-b6c2-1f3a8e9b5d24
description: Detects defense-evasion tampering of CloudTrail trails — StopLogging, DeleteTrail, or UpdateTrail calls that disable log-file integrity validation or change the S3 destination, as described in Unit 42's 'Blinding the Watchmen' research.
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cloud-logging-defense-evasion/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.001
  - attack.t1562.008
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection_stop:
    eventSource: cloudtrail.amazonaws.com
    eventName:
      - StopLogging
      - DeleteTrail
  selection_update:
    eventSource: cloudtrail.amazonaws.com
    eventName: UpdateTrail
  weakened:
    - requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation: false
    - requestParameters.s3BucketName|exists: true
  filter_error:
    errorCode|exists: true
  filter_service:
    userIdentity.type: AWSService
  condition: (selection_stop or (selection_update and weakened)) and not (filter_error or filter_service)
falsepositives:
  - Documented infrastructure-as-code change rotating trail configuration
  - Approved migration of logging destination during account consolidation
level: high
source:cloudtrail @evt.outcome:success (@evt.name:(StopLogging OR DeleteTrail) OR (@evt.name:UpdateTrail AND (@requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation:false OR @requestParameters.s3BucketName:*))) -@userIdentity.type:AWSService
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, userIdentity.type, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.userName, sourceIPAddress, awsRegion, requestParameters.name, requestParameters.s3BucketName, requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation, errorCode
| filter eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["StopLogging", "DeleteTrail", "UpdateTrail"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and userIdentity.type != "AWSService"
      and (eventName != "UpdateTrail"
           or requestParameters.enableLogFileValidation = "false"
           or isPresent(requestParameters.s3BucketName))
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
CLOUD

| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as trail values(All_Changes.src) as src_ip values(All_Changes.user) as user from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" AND (All_Changes.action IN ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail") OR (All_Changes.action="UpdateTrail" AND (All_Changes.change_type="audit" OR All_Changes.object_attrs.EnableLogFileValidation="false" OR All_Changes.object_attrs.S3BucketName=*))) by All_Changes.action All_Changes.object All_Changes.user All_Changes.src | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where user!="AWSServiceRoleForCloudTrail" | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.object) as trail values(All_Changes.src) as src_ip values(All_Changes.user) as user from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" AND (All_Changes.action IN ("StopLogging","DeleteTrail") OR (All_Changes.action="UpdateTrail" AND (All_Changes.change_type="audit" OR All_Changes.object_attrs.EnableLogFileValidation="false" OR All_Changes.object_attrs.S3BucketName=*))) by All_Changes.action All_Changes.object All_Changes.user All_Changes.src | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where user!="AWSServiceRoleForCloudTrail" | sort - lastTime
AWS S3 bucket deletion targeting an active CloudTrail log destination AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of the S3 bucket configured as a CloudTrail trail's destination — Technique 2 ('Delete Log Storage Destination') from the article. Pairs s3:DeleteBucket (and the prerequisite DeleteObject mass-empty) with a recent CloudTrail config showing the same bucket as target. High signal — legitimate workflows almost never delete an audit-log bucket. Rationale: Article calls out s3:DeleteBucket (with the prerequisite DeleteObject empty-pass) as Technique 2. The detection self-correlates by extracting S3BucketName from prior CloudTrail trail configs and matching against DeleteBucket targets — the article's note that 'a few minutes after the action, the trail will indicate this deletion' validates the temporal pattern.
ATT&CKT1485 T1562.008 T1070.007
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Decommissioning an old logging bucket after migrating to a centralized org-wide log archive
  • Lifecycle policy automation deleting a quarterly-rotated bucket once contents are archived to Glacier
  • Sandbox / disposable test account teardown via aws-nuke or terraform destroy
  • Compliance-driven re-region of the audit bucket where the old region's bucket is dismantled after migration
  • Vendor offboarding cleaning up a SIEM forwarder bucket
Suppression filter
| where UserAgent !has "aws-nuke" and UserAgent !has "terraform" and CallerArn !has "AWSReservedSSO_PlatformOps"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the DeletedBucket was an active CloudTrail destination (cross-reference DescribeTrails). Pull caller identity, userAgent, source IP; check change-management for an authorized decommission. 2) Contain: if unauthorized, apply an organization-level SCP denying s3:DeleteBucket on buckets tagged `purpose=auditlog`; revoke active sessions for the calling principal; if data still present in versioning, attempt MFA-Delete-recovery. 3) Hunt: search for prior DeleteObject/PutBucketPolicy/PutBucketAcl events on the bucket from the same principalId, look for s3:PutLifecycleConfiguration changes setting short expirations on other audit buckets, and review StopLogging events in the same window.
let LogDestBuckets = CloudAppEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(90d)
    | where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
    | where ActionType in ("CreateTrail", "UpdateTrail", "GetTrail")
    | extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
    | extend Bucket = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.s3BucketName)
    | where isnotempty(Bucket)
    | summarize by Bucket;
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType == "DeleteBucket"
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend DeletedBucket = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.bucketName),
         ErrorCode = tostring(Raw.errorCode),
         CallerArn = tostring(Raw.userIdentity.arn),
         UserAgent = tostring(Raw.userAgent)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where DeletedBucket in (LogDestBuckets)
| project Timestamp, DeletedBucket, CallerArn, UserAgent, IPAddress, CountryCode
| order by Timestamp desc

| extend DeletedBucket = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.bucketName),

         or (eventSource = "cloudtrail.amazonaws.com" and eventName in ["CreateTrail", "UpdateTrail", "GetTrail"]))

AWS CloudWatch Logs group deletion or retention shortened on audit-tier log groups AIActions on Objectives High
Detects DeleteLogGroup or PutRetentionPolicy calls that destroy or drastically shorten retention on CloudWatch Log Groups holding security-relevant data — the CloudWatch flavor of 'Delete Log Storage Destination' surfaced by reviewer feedback. Flags retention drops to 1 day on /aws/cloudtrail, /aws/lambda, GuardDuty, or VPC flow groups. Rationale: Reviewer extension of the article's 'Delete Log Storage Destination' technique to the CloudWatch surface. The article's framing ('blinding the watchmen' via log destination removal) maps directly to DeleteLogGroup; the PutRetentionPolicy ≤7d variant catches the stealthier 'shrink to negligible' approach. Naming filter scopes to security-relevant groups to control FP volume.
ATT&CKT1562.008 T1070.007
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • FinOps cost-cutting initiative shortening Lambda log retention org-wide via Config remediation
  • Re-deployment of an environment where IaC recreates log groups (Delete then Create within minutes)
  • Decommissioning an unused service's /aws/lambda log group during code cleanup
  • Test/dev sandbox automation that purges log groups nightly
  • Splunk/Datadog ingestion pipeline migration removing destination groups after switch
Suppression filter
| where CallerArn !has "finops-cost-remediation" and CallerArn !has "terraform-ci"
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the caller, source IP, and userAgent; verify whether the group held data that's been forwarded to long-term storage (S3 export) before being touched. Check IaC repo for matching change. 2) Contain: re-create the log group with original retention if subscription filters depended on it; restore from S3 archive if available; SCP-deny `logs:DeleteLogGroup`/`logs:PutRetentionPolicy` on `Name=/aws/cloudtrail*` resource patterns. 3) Hunt: pivot on the principal for prior `logs:DeleteSubscriptionFilter`, `logs:DeleteMetricFilter`, or alarm-disabling CloudWatch calls; look for parallel CloudTrail tampering (UC1) in the same session.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Amazon Web Services"
| where ActionType in ("DeleteLogGroup", "PutRetentionPolicy")
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend LogGroupName = tostring(Raw.requestParameters.logGroupName),
         RetentionDays = toint(Raw.requestParameters.retentionInDays),
         CallerArn = tostring(Raw.userIdentity.arn),
         CallerType = tostring(Raw.userIdentity.type),
         ErrorCode = tostring(Raw.errorCode)
| where isempty(ErrorCode)
| where CallerType != "AWSService"
| where LogGroupName has_any ("cloudtrail", "guardduty", "vpcflowlog", "audit", "securityhub", "/aws/lambda/")
| where ActionType == "DeleteLogGroup" or RetentionDays <= 7
| project Timestamp, ActionType, LogGroupName, RetentionDays, CallerArn, IPAddress, CountryCode
| order by Timestamp desc

title: AWS CloudWatch Logs Group Deleted or Retention Shortened on Audit Log Group
id: 7c4b9e2f-8a31-4c5d-9e1f-b3d7a6c4f218
description: Detects DeleteLogGroup or PutRetentionPolicy on CloudWatch log groups holding audit-tier telemetry (CloudTrail, GuardDuty, VPC flow, Lambda execution).
references:
  - https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/cloud-logging-defense-evasion/
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.defense_evasion
  - attack.t1562.008
  - attack.t1070.007
logsource:
  product: aws
  service: cloudtrail
detection:
  selection_delete:
    eventSource: logs.amazonaws.com
    eventName: DeleteLogGroup
  selection_retention:
    eventSource: logs.amazonaws.com
    eventName: PutRetentionPolicy
    requestParameters.retentionInDays:
      - 1
      - 3
      - 5
      - 7
  audit_groups:
    requestParameters.logGroupName|contains:
      - cloudtrail
      - guardduty
      - vpcflowlog
      - audit
      - securityhub
  filter_error:
    errorCode|exists: true
  condition: ((selection_delete or selection_retention) and audit_groups) and not filter_error
falsepositives:
  - Approved retention-policy tuning during cost optimisation
  - IaC pipeline recreating an ephemeral test log group
level: high
source:cloudtrail @evt.outcome:success (@evt.name:DeleteLogGroup OR (@evt.name:PutRetentionPolicy AND @requestParameters.retentionInDays:<=7)) @requestParameters.logGroupName:(*cloudtrail* OR *guardduty* OR *vpcflowlog* OR *audit* OR *securityhub*) -@userIdentity.type:AWSService
# log group: /aws/cloudtrail
fields @timestamp, eventName, requestParameters.logGroupName, requestParameters.retentionInDays, userIdentity.arn, userIdentity.type, sourceIPAddress, userAgent, errorCode
| filter eventSource = "logs.amazonaws.com"
      and eventName in ["DeleteLogGroup", "PutRetentionPolicy"]
      and not isPresent(errorCode)
      and userIdentity.type != "AWSService"
      and (requestParameters.logGroupName like /cloudtrail/i
           or requestParameters.logGroupName like /guardduty/i
           or requestParameters.logGroupName like /vpcflowlog/i
           or requestParameters.logGroupName like /audit/i
           or requestParameters.logGroupName like /securityhub/i)
      and (eventName = "DeleteLogGroup" or requestParameters.retentionInDays <= 7)
| sort @timestamp desc
| limit 200
CLOUD
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src_ip values(All_Changes.object_attrs.retentionInDays) as retention from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" AND All_Changes.action IN ("DeleteLogGroup","PutRetentionPolicy") AND (All_Changes.object IN ("/aws/cloudtrail/*","/aws/guardduty/*","/aws/vpc/flowlogs/*","/aws/lambda/*","CloudTrail/*") OR All_Changes.object="*cloudtrail*" OR All_Changes.object="*audit*" OR All_Changes.object="*guardduty*") by All_Changes.action All_Changes.object All_Changes.user All_Changes.src | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where action="DeleteLogGroup" OR (action="PutRetentionPolicy" AND retention<=7) | sort - lastTime
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(All_Changes.user) as user values(All_Changes.src) as src_ip values(All_Changes.object_attrs.retentionInDays) as retention from datamodel=Change.All_Changes where All_Changes.vendor_product="AWS CloudTrail" AND All_Changes.action IN ("DeleteLogGroup","PutRetentionPolicy") AND (All_Changes.object IN ("/aws/cloudtrail/*","/aws/guardduty/*","/aws/vpc/flowlogs/*","/aws/lambda/*","CloudTrail/*") OR All_Changes.object="*cloudtrail*" OR All_Changes.object="*audit*" OR All_Changes.object="*guardduty*") by All_Changes.action All_Changes.object All_Changes.user All_Changes.src | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Changes)` | where action="DeleteLogGroup" OR (action="PutRetentionPolicy" AND retention<=7) | sort - lastTime
GCP Cloud Logging sink disabled or deleted AIActions on Objectives High
Detects GCP Cloud Logging sink tampering — the article's 'Stop Logging' (sink update with disabled=true) and reviewer-suggested 'Delete Log Router' (DeleteSink) variants. Sinks are GCP's primary log-routing mechanism; disabling or removing them breaks log delivery to downstream buckets and SIEM exports. Rationale: Article explicitly names `logging.sinks.update` with disabled=true as GCP's 'Stop Logging' equivalent and includes the Figure 1 console confirmation. Reviewer extended to DeleteSink. Both methodNames are documented GCP Logging Admin API operations; resource.type filtering and principal-email allowlists for known IaC service accounts cut noise.
ATT&CKT1562.008
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform/Deployment Manager pipeline rotating sinks during config drift remediation
  • Org-level admin removing a deprecated sink that pointed at a decommissioned BigQuery dataset
  • Disabling a noisy debug sink while troubleshooting a logging pipeline cost spike
  • Migration from legacy v1 sink to v2 routing model
  • Disabling a sink in a sandbox project where no production data flows
Suppression filter
| where CallerEmail !has "terraform-ci@" and CallerEmail !has "logging-pipeline-sa@"
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull principalEmail, callerIp, and userAgent from the audit log; confirm the sink's destination (storage bucket / BigQuery / Pub/Sub) and whether downstream SIEM ingestion is now silent. 2) Contain: re-enable the sink (PATCH with disabled=false) or recreate from IaC; deny `logging.sinks.delete` and `logging.sinks.update` on the offending principal via IAM Conditions; rotate the principal's keys if it's a service account. 3) Hunt: search the prior 7 days for the same principal performing `logging.buckets.delete`, IAM grant changes (`SetIamPolicy`), or `storage.buckets.delete` on log-archive buckets; check for parallel CloudTrail tampering if the env is multi-cloud.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Google Cloud Platform"
| where ActionType in ("google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteSink",
                       "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.UpdateSink")
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend MethodName = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.methodName),
         SinkName = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.resourceName),
         CallerEmail = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         Disabled = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.request.sink.disabled),

GCP Cloud Logging bucket deletion (DELETE_REQUESTED state) AIActions on Objectives High
Detects deletion of a GCP log bucket — the article's 'Delete Log Storage Destination' for GCP, where logging.buckets.delete moves the bucket into a 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED grace state before final destruction. Catching this within the grace window allows recovery. Rationale: Article explicitly names `logging.buckets.delete` permission and the unique 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED state behavior. The grace window is operationally meaningful — early detection allows undeletion. Single methodName match is high-fidelity; filter on principalEmail excludes IaC service accounts.
ATT&CKT1562.008 T1485
Data sourcesChange.All_Changes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Terraform destroy on a sandbox project removing the _Default log bucket
  • Cleanup of legacy regional log buckets after consolidating to a single-region strategy
  • Project deletion cascade that wipes associated log buckets
  • Compliance-driven migration from per-project log buckets to a centralized aggregated bucket
  • Removal of a one-off debug bucket created during an incident investigation
Suppression filter
| where CallerEmail !has "terraform-ci@" and BucketName !has "sandbox" and BucketName !has "-test-"
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the bucket's purpose (production vs sandbox) via name + IAM bindings; pull principalEmail and callerIp; verify whether undelete is still possible (within the 7-day DELETE_REQUESTED window — call `gcloud logging buckets undelete`). 2) Contain: undelete the bucket if within grace window; deny `logging.buckets.delete` permission on the offending principal via custom role / IAM Conditions; rotate service-account keys if a SA was used. 3) Hunt: search for parallel `logging.sinks.update`/`DeleteSink` from the same principal, IAM policy changes granting Logging Admin role in the prior 24h, and storage.buckets.delete on log-archive GCS buckets.
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Google Cloud Platform"
| where ActionType == "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend BucketName = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.resourceName),
         CallerEmail = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         Severity = tostring(Raw.severity)
| where Severity != "ERROR"
| where CallerEmail !endswith "gserviceaccount.com" or CallerEmail has "compute@developer"
| project Timestamp, BucketName, CallerEmail, CallerIp, AccountDisplayName
| order by Timestamp desc
// Microsoft Sentinel — auto-derived from the Defender XDR hunt.
// Requires the Microsoft 365 Defender data connector (streams the
// advanced-hunting tables into Sentinel; Timestamp → TimeGenerated).
CloudAppEvents
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Google Cloud Platform"
| where ActionType == "google.logging.v2.ConfigServiceV2.DeleteBucket"
| extend Raw = parse_json(tostring(RawEventData))
| extend BucketName = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.resourceName),
         CallerEmail = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.authenticationInfo.principalEmail),
         CallerIp = tostring(Raw.protoPayload.requestMetadata.callerIp),
         Severity = tostring(Raw.severity)
| where Severity != "ERROR"
| where CallerEmail !endswith "gserviceaccount.com" or CallerEmail has "compute@developer"
| project TimeGenerated, BucketName, CallerEmail, CallerIp, AccountDisplayName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Unauthenticated WebSocket / HTTP 101 upgrade to phoenix_storybook playground routes AIDelivery Medium
Detects external clients negotiating a WebSocket (HTTP 101 Switching Protocols) against phoenix_storybook playground routes (e.g. /storybook/*, /_storybook). This is the article-specific entry point used by the unauthenticated psb-assign event handler for CVE-2026-8467 RCE. Rationale: Article states the playground accepts attribute values 'over WebSocket' from any 'unauthenticated user' and names the affected routes implicitly (story URLs with a Playground tab such as /storybook/core_components/button). HTTP 101 status on these route prefixes is the deterministic pre-exploitation signal. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1190 T1071.001
Data sourcesWeb Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Internal developers using storybook for component review from corporate IP space
  • Synthetic monitoring / Pingdom-style uptime probes hitting /storybook/*
  • Internal CI integration test runners that drive the playground UI
  • Legitimate frontend authors live-editing components against staging
  • Browser extensions or accessibility scanners crawling the playground
Suppression filter
| where csUserAgent !contains "Pingdom" and csUserAgent !contains "UptimeRobot" and csUserAgent !contains "site24x7"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the cIP and csUserAgent for the alert. Resolve the cIP — corporate VPN egress / dev workstation / partner is benign; cloud-hosting ASN, residential proxy, or Tor exit is hostile. Confirm whether phoenix_storybook is supposed to be reachable from this network segment at all. Step 2 (contain): If hostile or unexpected source, block the cIP at the WAF/edge and add a deny rule for /storybook* paths from non-management networks. Disable the playground endpoint on prod (`storybook: [playground: [enabled: false]]`) or upgrade phoenix_storybook to ≥1.1.0 immediately. Step 3 (hunt): Within ±5 minutes of the upgrade on the same host, look for beam.smp/erl/erlexec spawning sh/bash/cmd/powershell (UC3), HEEx-marker cmdlines (UC2), .beam writes to /tmp (UC5), and BEAM outbound to non-standard public ports (UC4). Snapshot the BEAM node before restart for memory forensics.
let LookbackPeriod = 7d;
let beamHosts = DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackPeriod)
| where FileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec") or InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec")
| distinct DeviceName;
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackPeriod)
| where DeviceName in (beamHosts)
| where ActionType in ("InboundConnectionAccepted","ConnectionInboundAccepted")
| where LocalPort in (4000,4001,4002,4003,4004,5000,8080,8443)   // common Phoenix listening ports
| where RemoteIPType == "Public"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, LocalPort, Protocol, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
W3CIISLog
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where csUriStem startswith "/storybook/" or csUriStem contains "/_storybook" or csUriStem contains "phoenix_storybook"
| where scStatus == 101   // WebSocket upgrade
| where not(ipv4_is_private(cIP))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, cIP, csMethod, csUriStem, csUriQuery, csUserAgent, scStatus, sPort
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Phoenix Storybook Playground WebSocket Upgrade From External Source (CVE-2026-8467)
id: 4b2e9c1a-7d3f-4a8e-9b2c-1f4e8d5a3c70
status: experimental
description: Detects HTTP 101 Switching Protocols (WebSocket upgrade) on phoenix_storybook playground routes — the unauthenticated entry point for CVE-2026-8467 HEEx template-injection RCE.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
author: Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/12
tags:
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1190
  - attack.t1071.001
logsource:
  category: webserver
detection:
  selection:
    cs-uri-stem|contains:
      - '/storybook/'
      - '/_storybook'
      - 'phoenix_storybook'
    sc-status: 101
  condition: selection
falsepositives:
  - Internal developer accessing storybook from a corporate workstation
  - Synthetic monitoring / uptime probes hitting the playground route
level: high

source:(nginx OR caddy OR apache.access OR aws.alb OR aws.elb OR azure.app_service.http_logs) @http.url_details.path:(*storybook* OR *_storybook*) @http.status_code:101
#event_simpleName=NetworkConnectIP4 ConnectionDirection=1
| LocalPort=/^(4000|4001|4002|4003|4004|5000|8080|8443)$/
| ContextImageFileName=/(beam\.smp|erl\.exe|erlexec)/i
| NOT cidr("10.0.0.0/8", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("172.16.0.0/12", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| NOT cidr("192.168.0.0/16", field=RemoteAddressIP4)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, RemoteAddressIP4, LocalPort, ContextImageFileName], function=count())
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/storybook/*" OR Web.url="*/_storybook*" OR Web.url="*phoenix_storybook*") AND Web.status="101" by Web.src, Web.user_agent, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where NOT cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/8",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("192.168.0.0/16",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("172.16.0.0/12",src) | sort - lastSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen from datamodel=Web where (Web.url="*/storybook/*" OR Web.url="*/_storybook*" OR Web.url="*phoenix_storybook*") AND Web.status="101" by Web.src, Web.user_agent, Web.dest, Web.url, Web.status | `drop_dm_object_name(Web)` | where NOT cidrmatch("10.0.0.0/8",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("192.168.0.0/16",src) AND NOT cidrmatch("172.16.0.0/12",src) | sort - lastSeen
HEEx / Elixir Kernel injection markers in BEAM-spawned process command line (CVE-2026-8467) AIExploitation High
Detects shell or interpreter command lines (spawned by beam.smp/erl/erlexec) that contain Elixir Kernel / EEx / Code.eval markers consistent with CVE-2026-8467 HEEx template injection. The injected expression is compiled via EEx.compile_string and evaluated via Code.eval_quoted_with_env, so System.cmd/2, :os.cmd, Kernel.apply, etc. surface in spawned-process cmdlines. Rationale: Article names the exact sinks (`EEx.compile_string/2`, `Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3`) and the example payload primitive (`System.cmd/2`). The injection breaks out of the attribute string via `foo" injected={EXPR} bar="` — the literal `injected={` token is a deterministic IOC of this specific CVE. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/e35379dfe2ef1a71b141899e36f431017c55265d • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1190 T1059
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer-run `iex -S mix` shell evaluating Code.eval_string against staging
  • Elixir release runtime config (runtime.exs) using Code.eval_string at boot
  • Custom Elixir admin task that legitimately invokes System.cmd from inside the BEAM
  • Mix tasks shelling out via System.cmd during a deploy
  • Test suites driving the playground locally (dev/test env)
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "iex" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine !has "mix test"
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Pull the full ActingProcessCommandLine and the parent BEAM process. If the cmdline contains `injected={` or unmistakable Code.eval_quoted of attacker-controlled strings, treat as confirmed RCE. Cross-check for an UC1 hit (WebSocket upgrade) within 60s on the same host. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host from the network, kill the BEAM node, and rotate any credentials/keys/env vars accessible to the Phoenix release (DATABASE_URL, SECRET_KEY_BASE, AWS keys, OAuth secrets). Upgrade phoenix_storybook to ≥1.1.0 or disable the playground. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep all hosts running BEAM for the same pattern over the last 30 days. Pull DNS + outbound NetworkConnects from the BEAM PID for the C2 (UC4). Inspect /tmp, /dev/shm and the release directory for dropped .beam modules (UC5).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| where ProcessCommandLine has_any ("System.cmd","Code.eval","EEx.compile_string","Code.eval_quoted","Kernel.apply",":os.cmd","injected={")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, SHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| where ActingProcessCommandLine has_any ("System.cmd","Code.eval","EEx.compile_string","Code.eval_quoted","Kernel.apply",":os.cmd","injected={")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, Hash
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: BEAM Spawned Process With Elixir Kernel / EEx Injection Markers (CVE-2026-8467)

status: experimental
description: Detects beam.smp/erl/erlexec spawning a process whose command line contains Elixir Kernel / EEx template-injection markers (System.cmd, Code.eval_quoted, EEx.compile_string, :os.cmd, Kernel.apply) — characteristic of HEEx template-injection RCE per CVE-2026-8467.
references:
  - https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
  - https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d

logsource:

  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '/beam.smp'

#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(beam\.smp|erl\.exe|erlexec|beam)/i
| CommandLine=/(System\.cmd|Code\.eval|EEx\.compile_string|Code\.eval_quoted|Kernel\.apply|:os\.cmd|injected=\{)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())

Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats summariesonly=true count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_name) as child_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam") AND (Processes.process="*System.cmd*" OR Processes.process="*Code.eval*" OR Processes.process="*EEx.compile_string*" OR Processes.process="*Code.eval_quoted*" OR Processes.process="*Kernel.apply*" OR Processes.process="*:os.cmd*") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort - lastSeen
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstSeen max(_time) as lastSeen values(Processes.process) as cmd values(Processes.process_name) as child_name from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam") AND (Processes.process="*System.cmd*" OR Processes.process="*Code.eval*" OR Processes.process="*EEx.compile_string*" OR Processes.process="*Code.eval_quoted*" OR Processes.process="*Kernel.apply*" OR Processes.process="*:os.cmd*") by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | sort - lastSeen
BEAM / Erlang VM spawns shell or interpreter child (post-RCE — CVE-2026-8467) AIInstallation High
Detects beam.smp / erl / erlexec spawning a POSIX shell, Windows shell, or scripting/networking LOLBin (sh, bash, cmd.exe, powershell.exe, curl, wget, nc, python). The injected EEx expression executes with full Kernel access so the typical post-exploitation footprint is a child process out of the Erlang VM — which never happens in a healthy Phoenix release. Rationale: Article confirms the injected expression executes with full Kernel access via Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3 — the practical EDR signature is the BEAM VM spawning a shell or LOLBin, which has near-zero legitimate occurrence on a Phoenix prod release. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1059.004 T1059.001 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Mix release start scripts spawning sh during boot (rare, baseline-able)
  • Porcelain / MuonTrap / Erlexec ports invoking helper binaries
  • Health-check probes that exec a shell script from the BEAM
  • Cron-driven Mix tasks that shell out
  • Distillery / Mix release hooks running bash on deploy
Suppression filter
| where not(InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("erl_child_setup","run_erl","mix release") and FileName in ("sh","bash"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Confirm parent ImageFileName is genuinely beam.smp / erl / erlexec and the child cmdline does not match a baselined release-boot or health-check pattern. Pull the BEAM listening port and confirm CVE-2026-8467 affected version of phoenix_storybook in mix.lock. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, kill BEAM, rotate all secrets in scope of the Phoenix release, and block egress from the host pending forensic acquisition. Patch to phoenix_storybook ≥1.1.0 or disable :phoenix_storybook from the router. Step 3 (hunt): For each affected host, pivot to UC4 (outbound C2), UC5 (.beam drops), UC2 (HEEx markers in cmdline) and audit IIS/nginx logs for the originating /storybook* request (UC1). Search the cluster for the same parent→child pattern across all BEAM hosts.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| where FileName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FileName, ProcessCommandLine, FolderPath
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("sh","bash","dash","zsh","ksh","cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","curl","wget","nc","ncat","socat","python","python3","perl","ruby")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

BEAM process outbound to new public destination or non-standard port (post-RCE C2) AICommand & Control Medium
Detects beam.smp / erl / erlexec initiating outbound connections to public IPs on ports outside the Phoenix release's normal egress set (HTTP/HTTPS/DNS/SMTP/EPMD). Once HEEx-injection RCE lands the attacker often pivots BEAM into reverse-shell C2 — a healthy Phoenix release rarely speaks ad-hoc TCP to arbitrary public ports. Rationale: Article confirms full Kernel access including Network primitives. EPMD (4369) and the release's documented egress set (HTTPS to APIs, Postgres, Redis) are excluded so the remaining traffic surface is C2-shaped. Sentinel uses an ImProcessCreate→ImNetworkSession join because ImNetworkSession does not carry process-image attribution columns. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1571
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Phoenix release calling a third-party API on a non-443 port (e.g. Stripe webhooks endpoint on 8443)
  • Erlang distributed cluster traffic on a non-default port
  • Outbound to a managed Kafka / RabbitMQ endpoint on its broker port
  • Health-check / metrics push to a SaaS observability endpoint on 4317 (OTLP) or similar
  • Self-hosted Elixir telemetry sink on a custom port
Suppression filter
| where not(RemoteIP in ("<observability-sink-ip>","<managed-kafka-broker-ip>"))
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Resolve RemoteIP/PTR + Whois. SaaS provider on the release's allow-list → tune. Cloud VPS / dynamic-DNS / Tor exit → treat as C2. Confirm CVE-2026-8467-affected phoenix_storybook present and cross-check for UC1 / UC3 within the last 6h. Step 2 (contain): Isolate the host, block the RemoteIP at the egress firewall, kill the BEAM node, rotate secrets, patch to ≥1.1.0. Step 3 (hunt): Run the same query org-wide for ≥30d. Pivot to PCAP / NetFlow on the egress edge for the same RemoteIP/port across other internal sources. Search authoritative DNS for any CNAME pointing to the C2 host.

| distinct DvcHostname;

| where isnotempty(DstIpAddr) and not(ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr))
| where DstPortNumber !in (80,443,53,25,587,4369,5432,3306,6379)

Erlang .beam compiled module dropped to /tmp, /dev/shm, or %TEMP% by BEAM runtime AIInstallation High
Detects beam.smp / erl / erlexec writing a .beam compiled-module file into a temporary or runtime location (/tmp, /var/tmp, /dev/shm, /run, or Windows %TEMP%). Successful HEEx-injection RCE per CVE-2026-8467 lets the attacker call Code.compile_string / :code.load_binary at runtime — the corresponding .beam artefact landing outside the release's _build directory is a strong persistence/secondary-payload IOC. Rationale: Article specifies Code.eval_quoted_with_env/3 evaluation with full Kernel access — that lets the attacker invoke :code.load_binary on attacker-supplied bytecode, which surfaces as .beam writes outside the release's _build/lib path. A legitimate Phoenix release should not be writing .beam files into /tmp or %TEMP%. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1505.003 T1190
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Elixir hot-code-reload / Distillery release upgrade writing temporary .beam files
  • Mix dependency compilation during a deploy that uses /tmp as build root
  • Test fixtures that compile and load a module from /tmp
  • Edeliver / Distillery upgrade tarball extraction touching /tmp
  • ExUnit isolated test environments compiling temp modules
Suppression filter
| where not(FolderPath has "_build" or FolderPath has "deps")
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Hash the .beam file (SHA256) and check against any known-good build manifest for the release. Decompile with `:beam_lib.chunks` / `beam_disasm` and inspect for shell-exec / network primitives. Confirm via cross-correlation with UC2/UC3 within ±10 minutes. Step 2 (contain): Quarantine the .beam artefact, isolate the host, kill the BEAM node before it loads more modules, rotate secrets, patch to ≥1.1.0. Step 3 (hunt): Sweep org-wide for any BEAM-written .beam outside the release _build directory in the last 30d. Yara-scan the artefact across the fleet. Audit `:code.get_path()` and loaded module list on every BEAM node for entries outside the release tree.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where FileName endswith ".beam"
| where FolderPath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/run/","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, FolderPath, FileName, SHA256, FileSize
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType =~ "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileExtension =~ "beam"
| where TargetFilePath has_any ("/tmp/","/var/tmp/","/dev/shm/","/run/","\\Temp\\","\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("beam.smp","erl.exe","erlexec","beam")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine, TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, TargetFileSHA256
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Vulnerable phoenix_storybook (>=0.5.0, <1.1.0) software inventory for CVE-2026-8467 AIReconnaissance High
Inventory hunt that surfaces every host running an affected phoenix_storybook release. CVE-2026-8467 is unauthenticated pre-auth RCE — the only durable mitigation is upgrade or disabling the playground, so a clean asset list is the first SOC artefact required. Rationale: Article states 'All versions of phoenix_storybook from 0.5.0 before 1.1.0 are affected' and assigns CVE-2026-8467. A version-range inventory query gives the SOC the asset list for emergency patching before adversaries scan. Cross-checked against: • https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-55hg-8qxv-qj4p • https://github.com/phenixdigital/phoenix_storybook/commit/56ab8464d4375fa52db806148a06cce126ad481d
ATT&CKT1518
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • mix.lock in a developer workstation's checkout (not a deployed app, but still patchable)
  • mix.exs in a sample/template repo that's never compiled
  • Pre-release / RC builds of phoenix_storybook 1.1.0 that show as 1.0.99-rc
  • Vendored dependency snapshot in a different project's deps directory
  • Archive of an old project no longer running
Response runbook
Step 1 (triage): Cross-reference the host list against the CMDB to separate production-serving Phoenix releases from dev workstations. For prod, immediately verify whether the storybook router scope is mounted (`scope "/storybook", PhoenixStorybook.Router do ... storybook_scope/0 end`). Step 2 (contain): Patch phoenix_storybook to ≥1.1.0, or disable the playground in config (`config :phoenix_storybook, playground: [enabled: false]`), or remove the storybook scope from prod router. WAF-deny `/storybook/*` from non-management networks until patched. Step 3 (hunt): For every host returned, run UC1/UC2/UC3/UC4/UC5 for the last 30d to confirm whether exploitation has already occurred. Add the CVE to the vuln-management ticket queue with a 24h SLA.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where CveId =~ "CVE-2026-8467" or (SoftwareName =~ "phoenix_storybook" and SoftwareVersion matches regex @"^(0\.(5|6|7|8|9)\.|1\.0\.)")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, OSPlatform, SoftwareVendor, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by Timestamp desc

| order by TimeGenerated desc

Data sourcesVulnerabilities DeviceInfo DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
// TVM tables are daily snapshots — pin a 1-day window so the engine
// partitions on Timestamp instead of scanning the full retention.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-8467")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where Timestamp > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId, VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

// Sentinel has no native TVM table. If MDE→Sentinel streaming is enabled,

DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)
| where CveId in~ ("CVE-2026-8467")
| join kind=inner (DeviceInfo | where TimeGenerated > ago(1d)) on DeviceId
| project DeviceName, OSPlatform, CveId,
          VulnerabilitySeverityLevel, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by VulnerabilitySeverityLevel asc, DeviceName asc

Microsoft June 2026 Patch Tuesday — exposure to 'exploitation more likely' critical CVEs AIWeaponization High
Tracks unpatched Windows endpoints carrying the four critical June 2026 CVEs Microsoft flagged as 'exploitation more likely' (CVE-2026-47291 http.sys, CVE-2026-42985 RDP Client, CVE-2026-44803 / CVE-2026-44812 Win32k-GRFX). Pre-exploit hunting — surfaces the attack surface so SOC can drive emergency-patch prioritisation before threat actors weaponise. Rationale: Grounded in the four CVE IDs Microsoft explicitly flagged 'exploitation more likely' in the article (CVE-2026-42985, CVE-2026-47291, CVE-2026-44803, CVE-2026-44812). Pivoting on DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities is the cleanest pre-exploit signal — the CVE strings are the article-specific anchor. Datadog/Falcon LogScale/CloudWatch left empty because MDVM telemetry isn't shipped to those platforms; cross-correlated with IsInternetFacing from DeviceInfo to prioritise http.sys exposure.
ATT&CKT1190 T1203 T1210
Data sourcesVulnerabilities.Vulnerabilities
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Stale TVM data on devices that already received the June KB but haven't refreshed inventory
  • WSUS-pending devices in a scheduled deferred-patch ring (e.g. pilot group, kiosks)
  • Devices with a Microsoft-documented workaround applied (http.sys binding disabled, RDP Client outbound blocked) but the binary still version-stamps as vulnerable
  • Air-gapped or maintenance-mode hosts intentionally lagging the patch cycle
  • Removed-but-cached entries from devices that have been decommissioned but not yet aged out of DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
Suppression filter
| where IsInternetFacing == true or Priority in ("1-http.sys-network-RCE","2-RDP-client-RCE")
Response runbook
1. Triage — for each CveId hit confirm exposure is genuine by checking DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities timestamp freshness and cross-referencing WSUS / Intune deployment rings. Filter to IsInternetFacing == true first; those are the operational priorities. 2. Contain — for hosts with CVE-2026-47291 (http.sys) on internet-facing IIS / WinRM, deploy the June KB out-of-band or pull the host behind a WAF / disable the http.sys binding until patched. For workstations with CVE-2026-42985 (RDP Client), push a firewall rule blocking outbound 3389/tcp to non-corporate destinations as compensating control. 3. Hunt — pivot each exposed DeviceId into DeviceProcessEvents for anomalous SYSTEM-integrity process creation in the prior 14d, DeviceNetworkEvents for unsolicited inbound 80/443/5985 traffic on http.sys hosts, and DeviceEvents for WER application crashes naming http.sys, mstsc.exe, or win32kfull.sys — early IOCs if a public exploit is already circulating.
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where Timestamp > ago(2d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-42985","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44803","CVE-2026-44812")
| summarize arg_max(Timestamp, *) by CveId, DeviceId
| extend Priority = case(
    CveId == "CVE-2026-47291", "1-http.sys-network-RCE",
    CveId == "CVE-2026-42985", "2-RDP-client-RCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-44803","CVE-2026-44812"), "3-Win32k-GRFX-RCE",
    "4-critical")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(Timestamp, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project Timestamp, Priority, CveId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, IsInternetFacing, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, RecommendedSecurityUpdate, RecommendedSecurityUpdateId
| order by Priority asc, IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc
DeviceTvmSoftwareVulnerabilities
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2d)
| where CveId in ("CVE-2026-42985","CVE-2026-47291","CVE-2026-44803","CVE-2026-44812")
| summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, *) by CveId, DeviceId
| extend Priority = case(
    CveId == "CVE-2026-47291", "1-http.sys-network-RCE",
    CveId == "CVE-2026-42985", "2-RDP-client-RCE",
    CveId in ("CVE-2026-44803","CVE-2026-44812"), "3-Win32k-GRFX-RCE",
    "4-critical")
| join kind=leftouter (DeviceInfo | summarize arg_max(TimeGenerated, IsInternetFacing, OSPlatform, OSVersion) by DeviceId) on DeviceId
| project TimeGenerated, Priority, CveId, DeviceName, OSPlatform, OSVersion, IsInternetFacing, SoftwareName, SoftwareVersion, RecommendedSecurityUpdate
| order by Priority asc, IsInternetFacing desc, DeviceName asc

mstsc.exe spawns unexpected child process — RDP Client RCE post-exploit (CVE-2026-42985 + 5 related) AIExploitation Medium
Hunts the post-exploitation footprint of the six June 2026 Remote Desktop Client RCE CVEs (CVE-2026-42985, CVE-2026-42992, CVE-2026-44799, CVE-2026-44801, CVE-2026-47289, CVE-2026-48563) where a malicious RDP server triggers code execution on the connecting client. Surfaces mstsc.exe spawning any process outside its very narrow legitimate-child allowlist (conhost / rdpclip / tabtip / mstsc). Rationale: Anchored on the six June 2026 RDP Client RCE CVEs named in the article and on the article's explicit attack-vector text: 'an attacker who controls a Remote Desktop Server could initiate a remote code execution on the machine when a victim connects to the attacking server using the vulnerable Remote Desktop Client'. mstsc.exe is the named client binary. The legitimate-child allowlist (conhost / rdpclip / tabtip / mstsc / WerFault) reflects observed baseline behaviour of the binary — any other child is high-fidelity. Joined with the preceding 3389/tcp DeviceNetworkEvents in the same InitiatingProcessId to surface the malicious RDP destination directly.
ATT&CKT1203 T1219
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Administrator launching cmd.exe / mmc.exe from inside an active RDP session — this fires on the SOURCE host, not the target, but rare cases where shell extensions / launchers tunnel back
  • Custom enterprise RDP wrapper or Citrix/VMware Horizon clients that re-parent helper utilities under mstsc.exe
  • WerFault.exe spawning when mstsc.exe crashes against an unstable RDP server (excluded)
  • Microsoft Remote Desktop Connection Manager (RDCMan) or similar wrappers launching helper exes through mstsc.exe
  • Antivirus / EDR sub-process scanners reading mstsc.exe memory via a temporarily-parented helper
Suppression filter
| where not (ChildImage endswith @"\RDCMan.exe" or ParentCmd has_any ("/admin", "/v:") and ChildImage endswith_cs @"\cmd.exe" and AccountName has "admin")
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the parent mstsc.exe command line and the preceding DeviceNetworkEvents 3389/tcp destination for the same InitiatingProcessId. Classify the RDP destination: corporate AD-joined / RFC1918 vs external public IP. External destinations during the post-Patch-Tuesday window are high-confidence RDP-Client-RCE exploitation candidates (CVE-2026-42985 et al.). 2. Contain — isolate the host via MDE network isolation / Live Response. Disable the user account and rotate their credentials; the child process executed under their token. Block the destination RDP server IP at the perimeter and submit it to threat intel. 3. Hunt — pivot the destination IP across the fleet for any other mstsc.exe outbound connections. Look for follow-on persistence on the victim (DeviceRegistryEvents Run/RunOnce/Services writes by the spawned child), credential access (LSASS handle opens, SAM hive reads), and lateral movement from the host (DeviceLogonEvents NetworkLogon initiating outbound).
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(14d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mstsc.exe"
| where FileName !in~ ("conhost.exe","rdpclip.exe","tabtip.exe","mstsc.exe","werfault.exe","werfaultsecure.exe")
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| join kind=leftouter (
    DeviceNetworkEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "mstsc.exe"
    | where RemotePort == 3389
    | summarize RdpDestIP = make_set(RemoteIP, 5), RdpDestUrl = make_set(RemoteUrl, 5) by DeviceId, InitiatingProcessId
  ) on $left.DeviceId == $right.DeviceId, $left.InitiatingProcessId == $right.InitiatingProcessId
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          ParentImage = InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          ParentCmd   = InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          ChildImage  = FolderPath,
          ChildCmd    = ProcessCommandLine,
          ChildIntegrity = ProcessIntegrityLevel,
          SHA256, RdpDestIP, RdpDestUrl
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith @"\mstsc.exe"
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\conhost.exe")
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\rdpclip.exe")
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\mstsc.exe")
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\tabtip.exe")
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\WerFault.exe")
| where not(NewProcessName endswith_cs @"\WerFaultSecure.exe")
| where not(SubjectUserName endswith "$")
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, SubjectDomainName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, TokenElevationType, NewProcessId, ProcessId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Suspicious child process spawned by RDP Client (mstsc.exe) — CVE-2026-42985 post-exploit
id: 8d9e4d2a-7b3f-4c1d-9e5a-2b6f1d8e7c4a
description: Detects mstsc.exe spawning an unexpected child process, an indicator of one of the six June 2026 Remote Desktop Client RCE vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-42985, CVE-2026-42992, CVE-2026-44799, CVE-2026-44801, CVE-2026-47289, CVE-2026-48563) where a victim's mstsc.exe connects to an attacker-controlled RDP server and is exploited.
references:
  - https://blog.talosintelligence.com/microsoft-patch-tuesday-for-june-2026-snort-rules-and-prominent-vulnerabilities/
  - https://msrc.microsoft.com/update-guide/vulnerability/CVE-2026-42985
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/06/11
tags:
  - attack.execution
  - attack.t1203
  - attack.initial_access
  - attack.t1219
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  selection:
    ParentImage|endswith: '\mstsc.exe'
  filter_legit:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\conhost.exe'
      - '\rdpclip.exe'
      - '\tabtip.exe'
      - '\mstsc.exe'
      - '\WerFault.exe'
      - '\WerFaultSecure.exe'
  filter_machine:
    User|endswith: '$'
  condition: selection and not 1 of filter_*
level: high
source:(windows.sysmon OR windows.security) (@EventID:1 OR @EventID:4688) @ParentImage:(*\\mstsc.exe OR *\\MSTSC.EXE OR *\\Mstsc.exe) -@Image:(*\\conhost.exe OR *\\Conhost.exe OR *\\CONHOST.EXE OR *\\rdpclip.exe OR *\\RdpClip.exe OR *\\RDPCLIP.EXE OR *\\tabtip.exe OR *\\TabTip.exe OR *\\mstsc.exe OR *\\MSTSC.EXE OR *\\WerFault.exe OR *\\WerFaultSecure.exe)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/^mstsc\.exe$/i
| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\(conhost|rdpclip|tabtip|mstsc|werfault|werfaultsecure)\.exe$/i)
| NOT UserName=/\$$/
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, UserName, ParentBaseFileName, ImageFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
| sort(field=_count, order=desc)

AKS pod with hostNetwork:true in non-system namespace — CVE-2026-32193 container escape risk AIWeaponization Medium
Surfaces Kubernetes pod creations carrying `spec.hostNetwork: true` in user / application namespaces — the prerequisite configuration the Talos article calls out for CVE-2026-32193 (Azure Kubernetes Service path-traversal RCE). Per the article, an untrusted hostNetwork-configured container can reach host-level services not intended for unauthenticated access and break out to the AKS worker node. Rationale: Grounded directly in the article's CVE-2026-32193 description: 'an attacker who can run an untrusted container configured with host Network could send specially crafted requests to a host level service... break out of the container and gain control of the AKS worker node.' The `spec.hostNetwork: true` predicate is the exact configurable named in the article. Namespace exclusion list reflects documented Kubernetes infrastructure namespaces where hostNetwork is legitimate (CNI agents, OPA Gatekeeper, AKS managed components). hostPID and hostIPC pulled into the projection because attackers typically chain these for fuller escape — not in the filter so a hostNetwork-only deployment still fires.
ATT&CKT1611 T1610
Data sources
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Prometheus node-exporter DaemonSet deployed to a `monitoring` namespace (legitimately uses hostNetwork to scrape node metrics)
  • Cilium / Calico CNI in a non-`kube-system` namespace (some installations namespace-isolate CNI components)
  • Istio CNI / sidecar-init DaemonSets configured with hostNetwork for transparent proxying
  • NodeLocal DNSCache deployed outside kube-system
  • Custom AKS log-collection agents (Fluent Bit DaemonSet, Datadog Agent) that legitimately need hostNetwork
Suppression filter
| where ServiceAccount !in ("prometheus-node-exporter","datadog-agent","fluent-bit","nodelocaldns","cilium","calico-node","azure-cni") and ObjName !startswith "node-exporter-" and ObjName !startswith "fluent-bit-"
Response runbook
1. Triage — pull the full RequestObject pod spec. Confirm whether `hostNetwork: true` is intentional for this workload (CNI / node-exporter / log-collector). Identify the User / ServiceAccount that created the pod and the parent Deployment/DaemonSet. Check whether the container image is from a trusted registry or an external untrusted source (the CVE-2026-32193 precondition is *untrusted* container). 2. Contain — if hostNetwork is unexpected for the namespace, `kubectl delete pod` and revoke the ServiceAccount's `pods/create` permission in that namespace. Apply an Azure Policy / Gatekeeper / Kyverno admission rule blocking `hostNetwork: true` outside an explicit allowlist namespace set. Roll the AKS worker node the pod ran on (assume compromise) if confirmed malicious. 3. Hunt — review AKSAudit for other privileged pod creations (`hostPID`, `hostIPC`, `privileged: true`, `securityContext.runAsUser: 0`, hostPath volumes mounting `/var/run/docker.sock` or `/`) by the same User / ServiceA
AKSAudit
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where Verb == "create"
| extend ObjResource = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).resource)
| extend ObjNamespace = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).namespace)
| extend ObjName = tostring(parse_json(tostring(ObjectRef)).name)
| where ObjResource == "pods"
| where ObjNamespace !in ("kube-system","kube-public","kube-node-lease","gatekeeper-system","calico-system","tigera-operator","azure-arc")
| extend Spec = parse_json(tostring(RequestObject)).spec
| extend HostNetwork = tostring(Spec.hostNetwork)
| extend HostPID = tostring(Spec.hostPID)
| extend HostIPC = tostring(Spec.hostIPC)
| extend ServiceAccount = tostring(Spec.serviceAccountName)
| where HostNetwork == "true"
| extend Caller = tostring(parse_json(tostring(User)).username)
| project TimeGenerated, Caller, ObjNamespace, ObjName, ServiceAccount, HostNetwork, HostPID, HostIPC, UserAgent, AuditId, _ResourceId
| order by TimeGenerated desc
source:kubernetes.audit @verb:create @objectRef.resource:pods -@objectRef.namespace:(kube-system OR kube-public OR kube-node-lease OR gatekeeper-system OR calico-system OR tigera-operator OR azure-arc) @requestObject.spec.hostNetwork:true
CLOUD
`kube_audit_index` sourcetype IN ("kube:apiserver:audit","kube:audit") verb=create objectRef.resource=pods 
| where NOT objectRef.namespace IN ("kube-system","kube-public","kube-node-lease","gatekeeper-system","calico-system","tigera-operator") 
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.hostNetwork output=hostNetwork 
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.hostPID output=hostPID 
| spath input=requestObject path=spec.hostIPC output=hostIPC 
| where hostNetwork="true" 
| table _time user.username objectRef.namespace objectRef.name hostNetwork hostPID hostIPC sourceIPs{} 
| sort -_time

Hades Campaign: Python drops Bun runtime to /tmp/b/ from oven-sh release AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades Campaign's stage-1 import hook: a Python interpreter (loading a compromised PyPI package's __init__.py) writing the Bun runtime ZIP and extracted binary into /tmp/b/. This is the malware's distinctive way to obtain a JS runtime in environments lacking Node. Rationale: Anchored on the exact paths from the deobfuscated __init__.py hook: `_b = _o.path.join(_T.gettempdir(), "b", "bun")` and `_z = _o.path.join(_T.gettempdir(), "b.zip")`. The Python+/tmp/b/ pairing is article-unique — legitimate Bun installs land in ~/.bun/bin/, never /tmp/b/.
ATT&CKT1195.002 T1059.006 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer manually testing Bun under /tmp during local debugging
  • Dockerfile builds that extract Bun to /tmp inside a build stage
  • CI cache restore steps that materialize a bun binary at a /tmp path
  • Engineer following oven-sh upstream install one-liner into /tmp
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessCommandLine has_any ("oven-sh install","curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install") and InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("curl","bash"))
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: confirm the parent Python process and which package's __init__.py triggered the import (check InitiatingProcessCommandLine working dir; correlate with pip install events in the prior 24h). Pull SHA256 of /tmp/b/bun and check VT. 2) CONTAIN: isolate the host (especially if it is a CI runner with cloud credentials), revoke any short-lived OIDC tokens issued in the runner's session, rotate AWS/Azure/GCP keys exposed to that workflow. 3) HUNT: pivot on the AccountName/DeviceId for `.bun_ran` flag-file creation (UC3), bun child process running _index.js (UC2), and any /proc/*/mem reads against Runner.Worker (UC5). Pull the compromised package list and check pip install history against UC6.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where ActionType == "FileCreated"
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/b/" and FileName =~ "bun")
   or (FolderPath has "/tmp" and FileName =~ "b.zip")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName has_any ("python","python3","python3.9","python3.10","python3.11","python3.12","pythonw.exe","unzip")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName=InitiatingProcessAccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where (TargetFilePath has "/tmp/b/" and TargetFileName =~ "bun")
   or (TargetFilePath has "/tmp" and TargetFileName =~ "b.zip")
| where ActingProcessName has_any ("python","python3","unzip")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256,
          ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine

Hades Campaign: Bun binary in /tmp/b/ executes _index.js payload AIInstallation High
Detects the Hades Campaign stage-2: the dropped Bun runtime at /tmp/b/bun invoked with `run _index.js` to launch the modular AES-256-GCM-decrypted payload. Distinguishes from legitimate Bun by both the unusual install path and the _index.js argument. Rationale: Article verbatim: `_s.run([_b, "run", _j], env=dict(_o.environ), check=False)` where `_b = /tmp/b/bun` and `_j` is the located `_index.js`. The combo of /tmp/b/bun executable path + `_index.js` argument is article-unique; legitimate Bun never runs out of /tmp/b/.
ATT&CKT1059.007 T1027 T1140
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Developer running Bun from a custom /tmp install during dev
  • Ephemeral container builds that stage Bun in /tmp/b/ for build steps
  • Internal CI tooling that intentionally drops Bun to /tmp/b/bun
  • Bun upstream test suites checking out under /tmp
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull SHA256 of /tmp/b/bun and compare to oven-sh-published v1.3.14 hashes — Hades campaign uses an unmodified legit Bun binary, so the file is benign in isolation; the signal is the path + _index.js arg. Inspect /tmp/_index.js content and the parent Python process's working directory to identify which PyPI package triggered it. 2) CONTAIN: kill the bun PID, isolate host, revoke any GitHub Actions OIDC tokens, rotate secrets exported to the workflow's environment variables. 3) HUNT: enumerate DNS queries from this bun PID (C2 lookup), file writes (modular blob staging), and cross-host pivot on SHA256 of /tmp/_index.js.

| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where (FolderPath has "/tmp/b" and FileName =~ "bun")
   or ProcessCommandLine has "/tmp/b/bun"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName,
          FileName, FolderPath, ProcessCommandLine, SHA256,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath,
          InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessParentFileName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImProcessCreate
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)

| where TargetProcessCommandLine has "_index.js"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername,
          TargetProcessName, TargetProcessCommandLine,
          ParentProcessName, ParentProcessCommandLine, SHA256

Hades Campaign: .bun_ran flag file created in temp directory AIInstallation High
Detects creation of the article's signature one-shot guard file `.bun_ran` in the system temp dir, written after the Bun payload runs once per boot to prevent re-execution. Extremely high-fidelity — the filename is unique to this campaign. Rationale: Article verbatim: `_G = _O.path.join(_T.gettempdir(), ".bun_ran")` and the closing line `open(_G, "w").close()`. The filename `.bun_ran` is a campaign-unique artifact — Google/grep returns no legitimate software using this exact name as a guard file.
ATT&CKT1480 T1027
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Detonation/sandbox runs of this same sample by an internal IR team
  • Threat researcher running deobfuscated POC on an instrumented box
  • Red team replaying Hades artifacts during a tabletop exercise
  • Backup/restore of a previously compromised host's /tmp
Response runbook
1) TRIAGE: pull the ContextImageFileName/InitiatingProcess and confirm whether the writer was python (matches campaign) or bun (less common but possible). Snapshot /tmp/_index.js, /tmp/b/bun, and the Python __init__.py that triggered the hook. 2) CONTAIN: isolate host immediately — guard-file existence proves the JS payload already executed, so credential-scraping modules have run. Force rotate ALL secrets reachable from this host (cloud keys, GitHub PATs, npm tokens, deploy keys). 3) HUNT: query the affected PyPI package install history (UC6), search for the SHA256 of /tmp/_index.js across the fleet, and look for outbound to github.com from non-developer hosts (potential exfil channel — same TA pattern from prior Miasma campaigns).
